journal_articles.title: A temporal single cell atlas of dynamic chromatin accessibility during murine lung maturation.
journal_articles.abstract: Lung maturation involves intricate cellular differentiation and structural remodeling, yet the underlying epigenetic dynamics remain poorly characterized at single-cell resolution. Here we present HTL-ATAC-seq, an ultra-high-throughput, ligation-based single-cell ATAC-seq approach. Applying HTL-ATAC-seq to mouse lung tissue across 15 continuous postnatal time points, we construct a temporal chromatin accessibility atlas of 1,185,619 nuclei, identifying 129 distinct cell subclusters and 713,987 candidate chromatin regulatory elements. Temporal analysis reveals three distinct cellular maturation stages and 12 dynamic chromatin accessibility patterns, capturing the transition from structural morphogenesis to immune maturation. We uncover distinct transcription factor regulatory patterns between alveolar type 1 and 2 cells and identify a putative Sprr1a enhancer specifically active in alveolar type 1 cells. Finally, we identify time- and cell-type-specific cis-regulatory elements associated with lung disease-related gene sets. In this work, we provide a comprehensive resource for understanding the epigenetic mechanisms underlying lung maturation and lung disease-associated regulatory programs.

journal_articles.title: Spatial multi-omic atlas profiles early organogenesis of a Carnegie stage 12 human embryo.
journal_articles.abstract: Organogenesis marks one of the most dynamic periods of early human embryonic development. Although the morphological features of this period have been described, the underlying transcriptional and metabolic landscapes remain poorly understood owing to the lack of an integrated spatial strategy. We present spatial transcriptomic and metabolomic maps of a Carnegie stage 12 (CS12) human embryo, co-registered with embryonic anatomy to generate a unified spatial multi-omic framework. Unsupervised clustering of the spatial transcriptomic data identified 17 cell populations covering the major organ primordia. Notably, we observed spatially separable hepatocyte- and cholangiocyte-lineage primed transcriptional programmes within the liver primordium, and detected cardiac outflow tract and sinoatrial node progenitors at CS12. Furthermore, integration of gene and metabolite abundance highlighted regional associations between transcription factors and metabolic pathways underpinning lineage specification. Our work presents a spatially resolved multi-omic atlas of a human embryo at the onset of organogenesis.

journal_articles.title: Multiplexed embryo profiling links cellular state to zygotic genome activation in single cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Multicellular self-organization depends on interactions across multiple length scales, yet mapping protein states at high spatial resolution in whole-mount embryos remains challenging. Here, we introduce high-throughput 3D in toto iterative immunofluorescence imaging (3D-4i) and a dedicated computer vision pipeline to quantify morphological and molecular features from subcellular to whole-embryo scales across hundreds of samples. Applying this pipeline to early zebrafish embryos undergoing mid-blastula transition, we determine the cell cycle phase for each cell across the embryo, and uncover the spatiotemporal dynamics by which global meta-synchronous mitotic waves transition to cell cycle desynchronization. Using statistical analysis, we find that the cell cycle phase is the major source of variability in transcription within a division cycle, and combining this with the analysis of key transcription factors and chromatin modifier state, included in our multiplexed dataset, enables accurate prediction of transcriptional output during zygotic genome activation in individual cells. Together, these findings establish 3D-4i as a powerful approach for quantifying multimodal, multiscale biological processes underlying multicellular self-organization.

journal_articles.title: Single-cell TimeLapse-seq reveals MTA is an essential retrotransposon orchestrating mouse zygotic genome activation.
journal_articles.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) are temporally activated during mammalian early embryogenesis and are closely linked to zygotic genome activation (ZGA), yet their nascent transcriptional dynamics remain incompletely resolved owing to limited sensitivity and maternal RNA background. Here, we develop single-cell TimeLapse sequencing (scTL-seq), enabling allele-resolved detection of nascent RNA in individual embryos. Applying scTL-seq to mouse ZGA, we generate a refined transcriptional atlas of genes and TEs and identify the pronuclear (PN) stage activated genes and TEs. We found that transcription at PN stage is largely contributed by the maternal genome and enriched for genes highly transcribed in germinal vesicle oocytes. Similarly, Mouse Transcripts type-A (MTA) elements are transcribed in oocytes and highly active in PN stage. MTA knockdown disrupts zygotic gene activation and dysregulates hundreds of TE subfamilies, resulting in 1-cell embryo arrest. Using nascent transcripts, we further identify 662 TE-driven chimeric transcripts and show that TEs are essential for regulating key developmental genes, including Nfya, Setd2 and Tead4. Finally, we identify maternal transcription factors, including NOBOX, as potential regulators of MTA activation. Together, our study provides a high-resolution nascent transcriptome landscape of mouse ZGA and reveals vital regulatory roles of MTA retrotransposon in orchestrating early embryonic development.

journal_articles.title: Multi-omics profiling of the choroid plexus reveals developmental cellular remodeling, early immune gene activation, and epithelial cell heterogeneity.
journal_articles.abstract: Brain development and function are influenced by the choroid plexus, whose dynamic cellular and transcriptional changes shape immune cell trafficking and cerebrospinal fluid composition. Here, we performed a comprehensive multi-omics analysis-including bulk and single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics-of the lateral ventricle choroid plexus across postnatal and adult stages in mice and rats. We identified changes in the choroid plexus cellular composition and gene expression profiles, including early and progressive activation of several immune related genes in main cell types from early postnatal to young adult stage. Epithelial cells exhibited developmental remodeling over time, characterized by distinct gene expression programs, locus-specific changes in chromatin accessibility, and cellular diversity. In addition, we uncovered an epithelial cell population characterized by a distinct transcriptional signature. Our study offers a comprehensive atlas of transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility in choroid plexus cells, providing a valuable resource to guide future research.

journal_articles.title: RUNX1-ETO oncoprotein levels determine the balance between endothelial reprogramming and pre-leukemic growth in a human ES cell model of AML.
journal_articles.abstract: In t(8;21) acute myeloid leukemia (AML), the RUNX1 DNA binding domain is fused to RUNX1T1 (ETO) producing the RUNX1-ETO fusion protein. We previously showed that t(8;21) leukemic stem cells aberrantly activate endothelial signaling pathways to initiate blast cell proliferation. Here, we employed a human embryonic stem cell (ESC) line carrying an inducible RUNX1-ETO transgene to determine whether endothelial signaling pathway activation depends on disease progression or is directly induced by RUNX1-ETO. Single-cell analyses demonstrate that RUNX1-ETO reprograms ESC-derived myeloid progenitors towards endothelial cells. We show (1) that endothelial reprogramming is RUNX1-ETO concentration-dependent and irreversible, (2) at similar RUNX1-ETO and RUNX1 expression levels, a sub-population of blood progenitors can escape reprogramming, and (3) keeps proliferating when co-cultured with endothelial cells. Our experiments highlight the role of cellular interactions in the maintenance of pre-leukemic cells and provide important insights into the earliest stages of genomic reprogramming by oncogenic transcription factors.

journal_articles.title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root.
journal_articles.abstract: Plant development is highly plastic, with growth and architecture continuously shaped by environmental conditions. Roots, for instance, adjust their development to local water, nutrient and soil conditions. Despite this plasticity, individual root cell types are generally viewed as largely homogeneous populations that progress along a single developmental trajectory1. Here we show that rather than progressing along a single developmental trajectory, most Arabidopsis root cell lineage trajectories exhibit a stereotyped bifid topology, as revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping. One branch is characterized by a transcriptional program that is shared across multiple cell types and enriched for genes associated with environmental responses, including abscisic acid (ABA) signalling. This state occurs reproducibly in a subset of cells across multiple cell types, independent of developmental lineage, thereby revealing an additional layer of root cell identity. It is conserved across Arabidopsis ecotypes and persists despite major perturbations in developmental identity. Moreover, it is reduced in ABA-deficient and ABA-insensitive mutants and becomes more prevalent under water-deficit conditions. Together, these findings reveal an additional layer of root cell identity that is superimposed on developmental lineage and its prevalence is modulated by environmental conditions. These results uncover a previously unrecognized source of environment-associated transcriptional heterogeneity shared across root cell types.

journal_articles.title: Short-term memory of past caspase activity biases cell elimination in vivo.
journal_articles.abstract: Apoptosis is triggered by the activation of Caspases leading to irreversible engagement in cell death. However, recent data outline numerous non-apoptotic functions of caspases as well as quite ubiquitous sublethal activation of effector caspases in vivo, opening the question of what drives the bifurcation between cell death and survival. Using quantitative live imaging combined with machine learning and optogenetics in the Drosophila pupal notum (a single-layer epithelium), we reveal the existence of a large heterogeneity of caspase activity thresholds between cells and distinct spatial domains with low or high sensitivity to caspases. We outline the central role of past exposure to sublethal caspase activity, which sensitises cells to apoptosis for several hours and reduces their threshold, and can bias single-cell elimination. Altogether, this work reveals the role of a cell's past history for apoptosis regulation in vivo, which can bias clonal selection and the spatial pattern of cell death.

journal_articles.title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19.
journal_articles.abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

journal_articles.title: SMURFs regulate mesendoderm differentiation through SMAD2-dependent ubiquitination of CDK9.
journal_articles.abstract: Precise control of transcriptional timing is essential during embryonic development, where dynamic gene expression programs govern lineage specification. Promoter-proximal pausing of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and its regulated release into productive elongation constitute a critical checkpoint in transcriptional regulation. Nodal, a transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) family morphogen, promotes mesendoderm differentiation through SMAD2-dependent transcription, in part by promoting cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9)-mediated release of paused Pol II. While mechanisms of transcriptional activation downstream of Nodal are well characterized, how this transcriptional program is attenuated during gastrulation remains unclear. Here, we show that E3 ubiquitin ligases SMAD Ubiquitination Regulatory Factor (SMURF) 1 and SMURF2 are critical regulators of SMAD2-driven transcription. SMURF1/2 ubiquitinate CDK9 and promote its proteasome-mediated degradation, thereby restraining CDK9-dependent promoter-proximal pause release and productive transcription of SMAD2-dependent genes. Loss of SMURF function stabilizes CDK9, increases its occupancy at SMAD2 target genes, and enhances Pol II pause release, thereby sustaining mesendodermal gene expression. These findings reveal a ubiquitin-dependent mechanism that restricts morphogen-induced gene expression and ensures timely developmental progression.

journal_articles.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf. In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

journal_articles.title: BEAR-GRN: Systematic assessment of single-cell multi-omics-based gene regulatory network inference methods.
journal_articles.abstract: Identifying regulatory gene interactions is inherently challenging as it depends on both the transcriptional and epigenetic landscapes. Multiple methods are proposed to infer gene regulatory networks (GRNs) using single-cell multi-omics data, yet the absence of a standardized benchmarking framework remains an obstacle to unbiased performance evaluation. Here we present BEAR-GRN, a systematic resource providing standardized datasets, curated ground-truth networks, and a unified computational pipeline for benchmarking GRN inference methods. Using BEAR-GRN, we assess state-of-the-art multi-omics GRN inference methods across paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets spanning human and mouse cell types. We evaluate accuracy against four complementary ground-truth definitions, alongside computational efficiency, output stability, and modality contribution. Although ground-truth choice profoundly influences performance, LINGER and DIRECT-NET show the highest overall accuracy and stability. Modality perturbation experiments reveal that current methods are predominantly RNA-driven, with chromatin accessibility contributing limited independent signal. BEAR-GRN enables researchers to evaluate existing and new GRN methods against established baselines.

journal_articles.title: Leveraging genomic deep learning models for the prediction of noncoding variant effects.
journal_articles.abstract: Characterizing noncoding variant function remains an important challenge in human genetics. Genomic deep learning models have emerged as a promising approach to enable in silico prediction of variant effects. These models include supervised sequence-to-activity models, which predict molecular phenotypes such as genome-wide chromatin states or gene expression levels directly from DNA sequence, and self-supervised genomic language models. Here we review progress in leveraging these models for noncoding variant effect prediction. We describe practical considerations for making such predictions and categorize the types of ground-truth data used to evaluate variant effect predictions, providing insight into the settings in which current models are most useful. Our Review highlights key considerations for practitioners and opportunities for improvement in model development and evaluation.

journal_articles.title: Neuroendocrine cells can originate from club cells, but this potential is normally suppressed by Hes1 during lung development and homeostasis.
journal_articles.abstract: The binary cell fate decision between neuroendocrine (NE) and club cell lineages is fundamental to lung development and epithelial homeostasis, yet the mechanisms that maintain these lineages remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that Hes1, a Notch target gene, maintains club cell identity by suppressing neuroendocrine differentiation. Lineage-tracing analyses revealed that Scgb1a1-expressing club cells give rise to NE cells following Hes1 loss during development and adulthood. Single-cell RNA sequencing of endogenous NE (eNE) cells and induced NE (iNE) cells generated by Hes1 loss uncovered substantial heterogeneity within the iNE populations and transitional cells expressing Notch-associated genes and keratins. Lineage tracing further showed that iNE cells integrate into neuroepithelial bodies (NEBs), and iNE cells reconstructed cell-cell communication networks that closely resemble those of eNE cells. These findings indicate that club cells, including Scgb1a1-positive club cell progenitors and mature club cells, retain latent potential to adopt an NE fate, which is normally suppressed by Hes1. Our results identify club cells as a previously unrecognized cellular source of NE cells and reveal a key mechanism that preserves epithelial lineage identity in the lung.

journal_articles.title: A modular synthetic promoter toolkit for programmable gene control in activated and chronically stimulated T cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Synthetic circuits that couple transgene expression to endogenous transcription factor (TF) activity enable cellular response to changing functional states. In T cells, antigen stimulation results in dynamic changes of transcription factor expression programs. Harnessing these endogenous TF dynamics for programmable gene control remains an important challenge in engineered T cells. Here, we develop a library of synthetic promoters (SPs) responsive to seven TFs identified through transcriptomic analysis of T-cell activation programs. These promoters couple endogenous TF activity to transcriptional output across a broad dynamic range of inducibility and basal expression. We quantitatively profile promoter performance in HEK293 and Jurkat cells, evaluate them for orthogonality, and integrate them into Boolean logic gate architectures and network topologies to minimize basal transcriptional leakiness and improve ON/OFF ratios. We test selected synthetic promoters in primary human CD8⁺ T cells, under endogenous TF regulation, and we further characterize the NR4A2-responsive promoter subset in vitro and in tumor-infiltrating engineered T cells in a melanoma xenograft model, demonstrating dynamic and reversible activation.Together, these results provide a modular SP toolkit of TF-responsive synthetic promoters for programmable transcriptional control in engineered T cells.

journal_articles.title: Absence of a prolonged macrophage and B cell response inhibits heart regeneration in the Mexican cavefish.
journal_articles.abstract: A balanced immune response after cardiac injury is crucial to successful heart regeneration, but knowledge of what distinguishes a regenerative from a scarring response is still limited. The Mexican cavefish Astyanax mexicanus provides a unique comparative model to study heart regeneration and scarring within a single species. Astyanax surface-dwelling fish are capable of heart regeneration, whereas, like the human heart, their cave-dwelling Pachón counterparts form a permanent scar. Using single-cell transcriptomics and immune perturbations, we identify two distinct and largely sequential immune mechanisms driving regeneration in surface fish. First, late-present macrophages are actively phagocytic, and pharmacological inhibition of phagocytosis disrupts scar clearance and regeneration. Second, B cells recruited from 7 days post-injury promote cardiomyocyte cell progression into mitosis, and their inhibition with Acalabrutinib significantly impairs cardiomyocyte proliferation and regeneration. This B cell-dependent mechanism is conserved in zebrafish. Our findings reveal two independent late immune mechanisms distinguishing regenerative from non-regenerative cardiac repair, offering insights for potential therapeutic strategies to enhance heart regeneration in mammals.

journal_articles.title: Epithelial NF-κB shapes protective Treg cell responses to restrain intestinal inflammation.
journal_articles.abstract: Inflammation resolution depends on coordinated communication between tissue compartments, yet how the intestinal epithelium shapes its immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, using colonic biopsies from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and mouse models enabling tissue-wide visualization of NF-κB activity, we combine single-cell RNA sequencing and secretome analysis to define epithelial communication during colitis. We show that, paradoxically, the NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory secretome of intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) is essential for recovery and prevents unrestrained inflammation. Mechanistically, epithelial NF-κB promotes CCL22-dependent regulatory T cell (Treg cell) recruitment and promotes a tolerogenic, pro-repair cell state, accompanied by induction of the lipid-metabolism-associated GDPD3 and CCR4. In UC, epithelial NF-κB is not uniformly activated but instead induces a selective pro-inflammatory transcriptional program while repressing targets regulating T cell recruitment. Thus, we identify dynamic epithelial-immune communication and demonstrate a protective IEC NF-κB-Treg cell axis important for resolution of intestinal inflammation.

journal_articles.title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association.
journal_articles.abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type-specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. By learning a cell-cell attention network, CellDiffusion adaptively identifies corresponding populations across batches. Our approach applies cell-specific correction in data integration, generating cell embeddings that align cells across batches while preserving intrinsic cell types and developmental trajectories. We validate CellDiffusion across various datasets, including the human endometrium, one of the most dynamic and complex tissues featuring extensive cellular and molecular changes with the menstrual cycle. This framework also improves other essential analyses such as label transfer, clustering, and trajectory inference. CellDiffusion represents a powerful paradigm for accurate single-cell transcriptomic integrative analysis.

journal_articles.title: Sequential TPRX1 and HERVL activation delineates a progression toward the totipotent-like state.
journal_articles.abstract: The in vitro induction of 8-cell-like cells (8CLCs) from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) provides a model to study the regulatory principles of totipotency and zygotic genome activation (ZGA). However, the cellular dynamics underlying 8CLC emergence remain poorly understood. Here, we generate a TPRX1-EGFP/HERVL-tdTomato dual-reporter hPSC line to resolve the stepwise acquisition of totipotent-like identity. We show that 8CLC induction follows an ordered trajectory in which TPRX1 activation precedes the emergence of TPRX1+HERVL+ cells, which most closely resemble the in vivo 8-cell embryo transcriptionally. Single-cell transcriptomics and time-resolved flow cytometry further define a continuous transition from the primed state through a TPRX1+ intermediate to the HERVL+ 8CLC state. CRISPRi and RNA-directed perturbations support functional contributions of HERVL elements and HERVL-derived RNA to this transition, while potential locus-dependent mechanisms remain unresolved. Together, these findings establish sequential TPRX1 and HERVL activation as a defining feature of human 8CLC induction.

journal_articles.title: Ablation of CDK6 and STAT5B rewires T cell developmental dynamics and prevents ALK+ lymphoma formation.
journal_articles.abstract: CDK6 and STAT5B are well-established oncogenic drivers, but their interplay during transformation remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that simultaneous genetic deletion of Cdk6 and Stat5b in an NPM-ALKTg/+ mouse model completely prevents tumor formation. Immature DN2/3 thymocytes are identified as the cellular origin of ALK-driven malignancy. Single-cell transcriptomics reveals a tumor-specific differentiation trajectory that is fully disrupted by combined Cdk6/Stat5b loss, coinciding with a developmental shift. We uncover shared transcriptional targets of CDK6 and STAT5B involved in cell-cycle regulation and apoptosis at the tumor initiation stage. In human ALCL cells, dual deletion of CDK6 and STAT5B induces context-dependent synthetic lethality, exposing a potential therapeutic vulnerability. A transcriptional signature derived from CDK6/STAT5B-dependent tumor initiation genes identifies a high-risk subgroup of ALCL patients with worse survival. Together, these findings establish a molecular link between thymocyte development, the crosstalk of CDK6 and STAT5B, oncogenic signaling, and clinical outcome in ALCL.

journal_articles.title: Generating protein hydrogels with customizable stress relaxation behavior via deep learning-driven entanglement design.
journal_articles.abstract: Protein hydrogels are promising artificial extracellular matrices (ECMs) for 3D stem cell and organoid culture due to their favorable stress relaxation behavior (a decrease in stress in response to strain). Inter-chain entangled motifs, in which different protein chains are interlaced, represent a powerful strategy to synthesize such hydrogels. However, designing these motifs with tailored properties such as binding energy remains a major challenge due to the difficulty of simultaneously controlling these properties while ensuring entanglement. Here, we introduce TangleDiff, a deep learning framework for the de novo design of homodimeric entangled proteins with programmable features. TangleDiff generates diverse foldable entangled sequences with an in-silico success rate exceeding 70%, markedly outperforming current models (~1%). By conditioning TangleDiff on inter-chain binding energy, we generate novel protein dimers whose binding energies closely match the specified ranges, with approximately 70% of successful designs conforming to expected values. We experimentally validate TangleDiff by designing nine homodimers targeting various binding energies; seven successfully form hydrogels, with stress relaxation dynamics correlated with specified binding energies. This work establishes a general strategy for entangled protein design, opening avenues for entanglement-based biomaterial innovation.

journal_articles.title: Integrated pangenomics and population genomics reveal climate adaptation and maladaptation in an East Asian tree.
journal_articles.abstract: Characterizing genomic variation in keystone forest trees is critical for understanding and predicting the adaptation and maladaptation of terrestrial ecosystems to global climate change. In this study, we integrate five high-quality genomes and high-depth whole-genome resequencing data from 222 individuals across 44 natural populations of Populus davidiana in East Asia. Our findings reveal that genome divergence strongly correlates with epigenetic and regulatory features, with variable genomic regions closely associated with dynamic transposon activity linked to epigenetic modifications. A population-scale genotype-environment association analysis identifies 10,372 adaptive single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and 1322 adaptive structural variations (SVs). Among these, a temperature-associated SV and a precipitation-associated SV undergo functional validation providing evidence of their roles in the expression of PdaMSL10, a mechanosensitive ion channel, and the transcription factor PdaWRKY40, respectively. Overexpression and RNAi experiments demonstrate that differential expression of PdaWRKY40 is strongly associated with drought sensitivity or tolerance, facilitating adaptation to diverse environmental conditions. Additionally, genomic vulnerability forecasts under future climate scenarios highlight the increasingly significant role of SVs in environmental adaptation. These findings advance our understanding of the genetic mechanisms underlying climate adaptation in non-model keystone species and provide invaluable genetic resources for breeding programs aimed at enhancing climate resilience.

journal_articles.title: LENG8 granule regulates alternative polyadenylation in mammals.
journal_articles.abstract: Membraneless organelles (MLOs) participate in multiple cellular processes and layers of gene regulation. Alternative polyadenylation (APA) represents a pervasive gene regulatory mechanism that generates distinct 3' untranslated regions (UTRs) in transcripts. However, whether specific MLOs exist in mammals to regulate APA remains largely unknown. Here, we unveil a nuclear body, termed the LENG8 granule (G granule), that functions as an active hub for APA regulation. LENG8 deletion induces extensive 3'UTR lengthening in both cultured cells and male germ cells. Mechanistically, phase separation-driven LENG8 granule formation facilitates LENG8-CPSF4 interaction and promotes the subsequent assembly of the cleavage and polyadenylation (CPA) complex, thereby favoring proximal poly(A) site usage in target transcripts. We further elucidate that YTHDC1-m⁶A landscapes orchestrate LENG8 granule formation/maintenance and target selection. Moreover, LENG8 granules exhibit spatial localization and functional crosstalk with nuclear speckles. Notably, the 3'UTR length of target transcripts correlates with LENG8 granule assembly and properties in a cell-type- and developmental stage-dependent manner. Our study establishes LENG8 as a critical regulator of mRNA 3' end processing and demonstrates that LENG8 granules modulate mammalian APA, advancing our understanding of MLOs-mediated poly(A) site selection.

journal_articles.title: Learning chemical-induced gene expression perturbations with WAVE.
journal_articles.abstract: Chemical-induced transcriptional profiles facilitate systematic characterization of compound-driven perturbations, offering critical insights into mechanisms of action, especially for compounds with poorly defined molecular targets. However, experimentally profiling gene expression across all combinations of cell lines and compounds is impractical, limiting the large-scale application of comparative transcriptomics in drug screening. To address this, we developed a deep learning framework named WAVE (Wave Action-of-Drug with Variational Encoder), which predicts gene expression profiles from chemical structures and the basal states of cell lines and single cells. By effectively integrating drug molecular representations and cellular basal transcriptional profile using a β-variational autoencoder (β-VAE) framework, WAVE accurately predicts untested chemical-induced transcriptional profiles. Leveraging this integration of cellular insights and molecular characteristics, WAVE excels in drug discovery and drug repurposing based on in silico perturbation experiment. It's application in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) drug discovery showcased its potential to identify potentially effective compounds. Our results demonstrate the utility of WAVE for elucidating mechanisms of action for potential drugs and enabling large-scale drug screening.

journal_articles.title: The EF1α promoter of cilta-cel drives a highly effective GZMK+ transcriptional program.
journal_articles.abstract: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) and idecabtagene vicleucel (ide-cel) are approved BCMA-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells approved for the treatment of multiple myeloma. Although the higher efficacy of cilta-cel compared to ide-cel may be related to its unique nanobody binding domain, the constructs also differ in their use of EF1α and MND promoters, respectively, to drive CAR expression. To elucidate the basis of cilta-cel's efficacy, we analyzed CAR T cells from 87 patients with multiple myeloma (50 cilta-cel, 37 ide-cel) using flow cytometry and single-cell multi-omics. Cilta-cel showed a 10- fold higher peak expansion and greater persistence, driven by an inflammatory GZMK⁺ T cell subset marked by EOMES expression and motif accessibility, but not exhaustion profile. In myeloma xenograft models, the EF1α promoter in cilta-cel, rather than binding domain, recapitulated increased tumor control, enhanced expansion, and GZMK transcriptional profile compared with the MND promoter (ide-cel). These findings suggest that the efficacy of cilta-cel is linked to an EF1α-driven GZMK⁺ transcriptional trajectory that supports both persistence and effector function.

journal_articles.title: cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level.
journal_articles.abstract: Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level. cPRIME employs prime editing to insert genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci, followed by the quantification of changes in variant frequencies at RNA (cDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) level. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci and reveal that synonymous marker edits - frequently used in prime editing screens - can themselves alter RNA processing and thereby confound the interpretation of variant effects. Taken together, cPRIME provides a platform for studying the post-transcriptional consequences of genetic variants in their genomic context and establishes a framework for the functional interpretation of RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

journal_articles.title: BATF condensation drives gastric cancer metastasis via chromatin association and transcriptional regulation.
journal_articles.abstract: While liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) is understood to be relevant with various types of cancers, the relationship between LLPS and gastric cancer (GC) remains ambiguous. In this study, we demonstrate that the basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) shows increased DNA-binding activity and expression in GC tissues and cell lines, based on assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (ATAC-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analyses. Additionally, in GC cells, BATF forms droplet-like nuclear condensates. Using combined approaches of chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq), ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq, we find that BATF condensation promotes its binding to the TM4SF1 promoter and enhancer regions, thereby regulating TM4SF1 transcription and prompting the TM4SF1-driven formation of focal adhesions and GC metastasis. Thus, we unveil a role for BATF LLPS in GC metastasis through its modulation of chromatin association and transcriptional regulation, highlighting the relevance of LLPS to GC progression and potential treatment approaches.

journal_articles.title: Disruption of SWI/SNF ATPases in the mouse liver impairs diurnal gene expression associated with specific promoter features.
journal_articles.abstract: Rhythmic gene expression is controlled by oscillating recruitment of specific transcription factors and co-regulators, including histone-modifying enzymes and chromatin-remodeling complexes. To unravel the significance of SWI/SNF ATPase subunits in diurnal chromatin remodeling, we have mapped diurnal chromatin accessibility, SWI/SNF occupancy, and gene expression throughout a day in the liver of male mice exposed to a night restricted feeding regimen. We find remarkable remodeling during fasting-to-fed transitions, and a third of rhythmic enhancers exhibited diurnal SWI/SNF occupancy and accessibility. Hepatocyte-specific disruption of either of the two mutually exclusive ATPases of SWI/SNF has minor effects on chromatin accessibility. However, simultaneous disruption of both ATPases results in a collapse of chromatin accessibility in the majority of distal cis-regulatory and a third of promoter proximal cis-regulatory elements, which leads to disrupted diurnal gene expression and signs of liver damage and inflammation. SWI/SNF-dependent promoters exhibit similarities with diurnal promoters, indicating a potential sequence-level bias that favors dynamic SWI/SNF-mediated chromatin remodeling. Collectively, this suggests an essential role of SWI/SNF-mediated chromatin remodeling of cis-regulatory regions for rhythmic gene expression and basic liver function.

journal_articles.title: Neoplastic and non-neoplastic astrocyte states converge on mesenchymal and injury-response programs during glioblastoma recurrence.
journal_articles.abstract: Glioblastomas initially respond to radiotherapy but invariably recur, often within high-dose radiation treatment fields. Although stromal radiation responses are incompletely understood, evidence suggests that the tumor microenvironment becomes tumor-supportive after therapy. Using a genetically engineered glioblastoma mouse model, we profiled healthy brain, primary tumors, and post-radiotherapy recurrences with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence. Across 13 non-neoplastic cell types and 10 tumor cell states, we mapped transcriptional adaptations accompanying progression from healthy brain to primary and recurrent glioblastoma. We find distinct astrocyte states linked to disease stage, including reactive, non-neoplastic astrocytes and tumor cells adopting reactive astrocyte-like phenotypes. Reactive astrocyte-like tumor cells with mesenchymal and injury-response signatures are enriched after radiotherapy and persist in recurrent tumors. Receptor-ligand interactions between reactive astrocytes and tumor cells include known and putative drivers of aggressiveness. These findings highlight convergent reactive astrocyte programs in astrocytes and tumor cells as potential mediators of glioblastoma radioresistance.

journal_articles.title: Development-inspired approach for the derivation of functional and transplantable salivary gland organoids from human pluripotent stem cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Salivary gland (SG) hypofunction significantly affects the life quality of patients with hyposalivation. Current treatment options for these conditions are limited and often result in undesirable side effects. To address this issue, we've developed a developmentally inspired strategy to derive salivary gland epithelial progenitor (SGEP) cells from human pluripotent stem cells (PSC). Then we employ SGEP cells derived from human PSC with a SOX10::GFP reporter to engineer three-dimensional lumenized SG organoids, with well-defined lumens and secretory function, reminiscent of human salivary glands. Upon transplantation into the submandibular gland of athymic nude mice, mCherry+ salivary gland organoids (SGO) integrate into the gland and differentiated into salivary gland phenotypes, including acinar, ductal and myoepithelial structures. Our findings suggest that SG organoids may hold promise for studying SG development, disease progression and drug screening, as well as for development of cell therapies for salivary gland regeneration.

journal_articles.title: Three-dimensional chromatin architecture is rapidly restored after DNA replication.
journal_articles.abstract: Studies of post-replicative chromatin exclusively focus on the kinetics of protein binding after DNA replication to understand maintenance of transcriptional programs. Here we investigated both chromatin-bound factors and the three-dimensional architecture of the post-replicative genome in human cells. We found that transcription factors and chromatin looping proteins rapidly associate with nascent DNA. We discovered that the architectural factors, CTCF and YY1, bind to their target sequences immediately following DNA replication, and that chromatin loops from 39 to 425 kb re-form within 10 min of DNA replication. This suggests that the 3D structure of chromatin is at most briefly disrupted by DNA replication and quickly restores following replisome passage, providing insight into an unaddressed question of the structure of post-replicated chromatin. Our results suggest that all components of the transcriptional network and tertiary chromatin structure are restored shortly after replication, which is consistent with previously detected fast resumption of transcription on daughter DNA strands.

journal_articles.title: Topology-enhanced machine learning for speech signal processing.
journal_articles.abstract: In artificial-intelligence-aided signal processing, existing deep learning models often exhibit a black-box structure. Here, conceptually beyond spectral analysis, we demonstrate that topological methods not only effectively capture intrinsic and complex structural information but can also enhance neural networks. We provide a transparent methodology, TopCap, to capture topological features inherent in time series for basic machine learning. Compared to prior approaches, we obtain descriptors that probe finer information such as the vibration of a time series. Notably, in classifying voiced and voiceless consonants, TopCap achieves an accuracy consistently standing in comparison with neural network models. Moreover, by integrating TopCap features into those neural networks, our approach improves upon state-of-the-art methods in terms of robustness against noise, as well as accuracy, stability, convergence of loss function, and interpretability.

journal_articles.title: Establishing Polycomb regulatory landscapes in human early development.
journal_articles.abstract: H2AK119ub (H2Aub) and H3K27me3, which are deposited by the Polycomb group (PcG) complexes PRC1 and PRC2, respectively, cooperatively repress developmental genes. However, in human preimplantation embryos, H3K27me3 undergoes genome-wide erasure and subsequent restoration. How H3K27me3 is reestablished and whether PcG complexes still regulate gene repression in human embryos remain unknown. Here, we profiled H2Aub dynamics from human gametes to blastocysts. H2Aub emerges in GC-rich regions as early as the two-cell stage, progressively accumulates at both active and inactive genes, and further culminates at PcG targets in later stages. H3K27me3 is weakly correlated with H2Aub in oocytes and two-cell embryos but colocalizes with H2Aub at H3K4me3-depleted, inactive PcG targets in blastocysts. Loss of H2Aub abolishes H3K27me3 reestablishment at PcG targets causing moderate derepression, accompanied by ectopic H3K27me3 deposition and impaired embryonic development. Finally, H2Aub and DNA methylation cooperatively maintain H3K27me3 patterning in human embryonic stem cells. Therefore, H2Aub-dependent H3K27me3 deposition underlies the earliest establishment of Polycomb repression in humans.

journal_articles.title: Cell and nuclear scaling constrains tissue fluidity in a doubly-dense remodeling epithelium.
journal_articles.abstract: During epithelial remodeling, tissues exhibit solid- or fluid-like properties depending on developmental constraints. In soft matter systems like foams and colloidal glasses, component size influences material mechanics. Here, we investigated how cell and nuclear size affect tissue mechanics. mh mutant embryos have epithelia with doubled cell densities, creating cells with altered 3D aspect ratios. Nuclear volumes scale non-linearly with cell volumes, adopting rounder shapes and reduced apical-basal heights, suggesting that stiff nuclei deform less than cell cortices. These compacted nuclei resemble a jammed state, reducing tissue fluidity and impairing extension movements. Interestingly, oscillatory amplitudes and frequencies in mh cells are comparable to control despite their reduced size, demonstrating an uncoupling between biochemical oscillation machinery and cell dimensions. Additionally, though planar-polarized magnitudes are dampened, the angular assignment of interfacial behaviors is preserved, suggesting that this planar informational system still operates with high fidelity despite reduced cell dimensions. Thus, these results indicate that development has fine-tuned epithelial dimensions to work at time-scales compatible with embryonic requirements.

journal_articles.title: Msps/XMAP215 Is Essential for Oocyte Specification in the Drosophila Ovary.
journal_articles.abstract: Cell fate determination is fundamental to development. In the Drosophila ovary, a 16-cell germline cyst forms in which two pro-oocytes arise; one of the pro-oocytes is selected as the oocyte, while the remaining 15 cells differentiate into nurse cells. Here, we identify Mini spindles (Msps), a Drosophila XMAP215-family microtubule polymerase, as a key regulator of oocyte fate specification. msps mRNA and Msps protein are enriched in the pro-oocytes prior to oocyte specification. Elimination of Msps prevents oocyte specification and disrupts the accumulation of the oocyte marker Orb, producing egg chambers with 16 nurse cells. Conversely, optogenetic recruitment of Msps increases microtubule polymerization and promotes Orb accumulation in nurse cells, suggesting that Msps activity is sufficient to initiate key molecular events associated with oocyte specification. Furthermore, Msps associates with the germline-specific organelles, the spectrosome and fusome, and becomes asymmetrically distributed, biasing the two pro-oocytes toward oocyte fate. We propose that an Msps-dynein feedback loop amplifies small initial differences between the two pro-oocytes to specify a single oocyte.

journal_articles.title: Automated screening of autism via a pretrained vision-language model in naturalistic caregiver-child interactions.
journal_articles.abstract: Early autism screening is essential for timely intervention but remains constrained by specialist dependence, costly protocols, and limited accessibility. We present Autism-CLIP, a vision-language model that automates screening from 3-min naturalistic caregiver-child interaction videos recorded in toddlers aged 15-24 months. By integrating contrastive learning, large language model-generated supervision, domain-specific architecture, and hybrid training, Autism-CLIP aligns visual behavioral cues with autism-related assessment outcomes, enabling annotation-free inference. In multicenter evaluation, Autism-CLIP achieved an AUC of 0.903 in the internal cohort (n = 103) and 0.873 in the external cohort (n = 102), outperforming conventional machine learning methods. Attention mapping highlighted clinically relevant markers, including gaze aversion and limited social reciprocity. Requiring only smartphone-captured videos without manual coding or controlled settings, Autism-CLIP offers a scalable, low-cost approach to broaden access to early autism screening and support prioritization of clinical resources.

journal_articles.title: Bayesian bilevel operator learning with low-rank adaptation for efficient uncertainty quantification of PDE inverse problems.
journal_articles.abstract: Uncertainty quantification in PDE inverse problems is essential in many applications. Scientific machine learning and AI enable data-driven learning of model components while preserving physical structure, and provide the scalability and adaptability needed for emerging imaging technologies and clinical insights. We develop a Bilevel Local Operator Learning framework for Bayesian inference in PDEs (B-BiLO). At the upper level, we sample parameters from the posterior via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, while at the lower level we fine-tune a neural network via low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to approximate the solution operator locally. B-BiLO enables efficient gradient-based sampling without synthetic data or adjoint equations and avoids sampling in high-dimensional weight space, as in Bayesian neural networks, by optimizing weights deterministically. We analyze errors from approximate lower-level optimization and establish their impact on posterior accuracy. Numerical experiments across PDE models, including tumor growth, demonstrate that B-BiLO achieves accurate and efficient uncertainty quantification.

journal_articles.title: Deep learning coupled with scalable domain-specific structural validation expands RNA virus discovery from metatranscriptomes.
journal_articles.abstract: The discovery of RNA viruses from metatranscriptomic data remains challenging due to extreme sequence divergence and length heterogeneity, ranging from massive polyproteins to short assembly artifacts. We present Rider, a two-stage framework that synergizes deep representation learning with scalable domain-specific structural validation. In the first stage, Rider leverages a compact pretrained protein language model to broadly detect highly divergent viral signals. To overcome the inherent input length limitations of language models and accurately capture catalytic core domains, the second stage employs an overlapping sliding-window structure prediction strategy. These structures are then aligned against our curated database of non-redundant RdRp (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) domains. This domain-centric design detects RdRp domains embedded within long polyproteins and truncated fragments. Across >10,000 metatranscriptomes spanning diverse ecosystems, Rider achieves sensitivity comparable to LucaProt, recalling >99% of previously cataloged RNA viruses. Rider identifies thousands of deeply divergent sequences and clades that elude existing methods. In a human inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) cohort, Rider agrees with other methods in detecting RNA viruses while extending detection to divergent lineages, providing a scalable pipeline for global RNA virome exploration.

journal_articles.title: Histone deacetylase inhibition induces an antitumor IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in macrophages.
journal_articles.abstract: Epigenetic reprogramming underlies innate immune memory. However, whether trained immunity can be induced via epigenetic intervention to combat tumors, and the key regulators controlling this process, remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that histone deacetylase inhibitor (HDACi) priming establishes a trained immunity-like state in monocytes/macrophages, conferring potent antitumor effect in multiple models of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) in female mice. Interferon regulatory factor 8 (IRF8) is identified as the master regulator of the inflammatory transcriptional program, which is governed by IRF8-associated super-enhancers and reinforced by HDACi. Myeloid-specific IRF8 deficiency impairs pro-inflammatory macrophage differentiation and abrogates HDACi-induced antitumor efficacy. Moreover, an IRF8-driven, CCL8-expressing macrophage subset recruits and activates cytotoxic CCR5+CD8+ T cells in the TNBC microenvironment. As a proof-of-principle with translational relevance, CCL8-overexpressing EGFR-targeted CAR T cells exhibit enhanced trafficking and improved efficacy in a humanized TNBC model. Our study defines the IRF8-CCL8-CCR5 axis as an epigenetically potentiated nexus of innate and adaptive antitumor immunity.

journal_articles.title: Oropouche virus disrupts neurodevelopment and exhibits congenital infection potential.
journal_articles.abstract: Oropouche virus (OROV) historically caused a self-limiting disease, yet recent strains have been clinically linked to congenital infection and neurodevelopmental disease. These observations highlight the need to study OROV as a congenital pathogen. Here, using both a historical and currently circulating strain, we show OROV infects neurons across differentiation states in human forebrain organoids. Compared with the neurotropic congenital pathogen Zika virus (ZIKV), OROV exhibits a heightened capacity for neuroinfection and pathology in both forebrain organoids and neonatal mice. The increased permissiveness of OROV is driven, in part, by a broader neuronal tropism and a relative insensitivity to neuronal type I interferon-mediated antiviral responses. Consistent with clinical observations, neonatal neuroinfection results in rapid and severe neuropathology marked by cerebral hemorrhage. Finally, using a transient type I interferon-blockade model, we demonstrate that OROV can productively infect the murine placenta and cause fetal growth restriction. Together, our complementary models support a unified framework in which placental and fetal barriers limit productive fetal brain infection, yet OROV exhibits marked neurotropism and neuropathogenic potential upon gaining access to developing neural tissues. These findings reinforce the need for vigilant monitoring of OROV as an emerging pathogen associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and congenital disease.

journal_articles.title: Tissue composition shapes differential skeletal integration strategies during axolotl limb regeneration.
journal_articles.abstract: Limb regeneration requires rebuilding the missing structures and integrating them with stump tissues. Osteoclast-mediated tissue resorption is essential for skeletal integration during regeneration. However, it is unknown if skeletal tissue composition impacts its resorption and, if so, how it is regulated. Here, we show that osteoclast-mediated skeletal resorption is activated in amputations damaging the diaphysis, but not the epiphysis, of skeletal elements. We found that amputations in the calcified diaphysis trigger the sustained expression of RANKL and the chemokine Loc483, and that the latter is sufficient to induce osteoclast presence in non-resorbing amputations. Finally, our data suggests that the transcriptomic profile of the apical epithelial cap is impacted by the tissues injured by the amputation. Overall, our work reveals that tissue composition at the amputation plane shapes adaptations of the regenerative program, which ultimately contribute to the near-seamless tissue integration of the regenerating axolotl limb regardless of the amputation position.

journal_articles.title: RanGAP1 coordinates the ER-lamina interface to drive de novo nuclear envelope reassembly in mouse embryos.
journal_articles.abstract: Nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly is essential for the zygote-to-totipotency transition in mammalian embryos. Beyond its classical roles in nuclear transport and maintenance of the RanGTP gradient, the function of RanGAP1 in embryonic NE reassembly has remained elusive. Here, we show that RanGAP1 localizes to the early embryonic NE, driving reassembly via a distinct structural mechanism. Trim-Away-mediated RanGAP1 depletion causes two-cell stage arrest and severe NE defects, including nuclear pore complex (NPC) loss, failed reassembly, and aberrant "fishnet" membrane structures. Mechanistically, RanGAP1 establishes a structural paradigm for endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-lamina coupling by recruiting Lamin A/C, B1, and B2 to the ER for coassembly. The acidic domain and SUMO-1 modification at Lys526 (K526) are essential for the NPC localization of RanGAP1. Thus, RanGAP1 orchestrates nuclear lamina (NL) assembly by targeting lamins to the ER. These findings uncover mechanisms of NE reassembly that are critical for early embryogenesis and provide insights into NE-related developmental disorders.

journal_articles.title: An engineered probiotic for diagnosis and mucosal healing in inflammatory bowel disease.
journal_articles.abstract: Early diagnosis and timely treatment of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are critical to limit disease progression, yet integrated diagnostic-therapeutic strategies remain limited. Here, we design a synthetic probiotic system that responds to reactive oxygen species (ROS) to enable noninvasive detection of intestinal inflammation. We further engineer EcN-IL22, a therapeutic strain that conditionally expresses interleukin 22-fragment crystallizable (IL-22-Fc) fusion protein in situ to mitigate colitis-associated tissue damage. Mechanistically, EcN-IL22 activates epithelial IL-22 receptor 1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (IL-22R1/STAT3) signaling, promoting epithelial barrier restoration and intestinal stem cell proliferation. We identify thyroid hormone receptor-interacting protein 13 (Trip13) and fidgetin-like 1 (Fignl1) as IL-22R1-responsive candidate genes associated with epithelial repair. Importantly, replacing the diagnostic output of the ROS-responsive circuit with IL-22-Fc enables inflammation-triggered therapeutic delivery and significantly alleviates colitis. Finally, EcN-IL22 demonstrates robust protective efficacy in a piglet colitis model, supporting its translational potential. Together, this work establishes an integrated probiotic platform for IBD diagnosis and regenerative therapy.

journal_articles.title: METTL4 interacts with histone methylation readers MRG1/2 to regulate alternative splicing and promote thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis.
journal_articles.abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) functions in thermomorphogenesis, but how AS is regulated during this process remains unclear. Here we show that METTL4 physically interacts with MRG1/2 in Arabidopsis thaliana. The mettl4-1, mrg1 mrg2, and mettl4 mrg1 mrg2 mutants exhibit reduced hypocotyl elongation under warm temperature conditions (28°C), indicating that METTL4 and MRG1/2 cooperatively promote thermomorphogenesis. Transcriptome analysis revealed that both METTL4 and MRG1/2 are required for warm temperature-induced reprogramming of gene transcription and AS. Further analysis showed that METTL4 and MRG1/2 modulate the AS of key brassinosteroid (BR)-signaling genes BES1, GSK1, and SBI1 in thermomorphogenesis. In addition, METTL4 promotes MRG2 binding to the chromatin of BES1 and GSK1 loci. METTL4 also promotes hypocotyl elongation and regulates the AS of BR signaling genes independently of its methyltransferase activity. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that METTL4 and MRG1/2 co-regulate AS and BR signaling to promote thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis.

journal_articles.title: Pharmacological blockade of p65 palmitoylation modulates NF-κB transcriptional activity.
journal_articles.abstract: Nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) regulates inflammation and immunity and is frequently dysregulated in autoimmune diseases, inflammatory disorders, and cancers. Cytokines and pathogens activate NF-κB transcription factors, and nutrients and metabolites, including fatty acids, also modulate its activation, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we report that RelA (p65), a major component of the NF-κB transcription complex, is autopalmitoylated at cysteine 197 and 206. Palmitoylation of p65 enhances its nuclear localization and p65-p50 complex formation, thereby increasing NF-κB transcriptional activities. We further show that licochalcone D, a small-molecule anti-inflammatory compound, directly inhibits RelA/p65 autopalmitoylation, suggesting it may act through an additional mechanism. These results indicate that fatty acid metabolism can directly regulate NF-κB activity through p65 palmitoylation and suggest that targeting p65 autopalmitoylation may be a therapeutic strategy for diseases with dysregulated NF-κB signaling.

journal_articles.title: Single-cell analyses reveal lymph node-tumor ecosystem remodeling during lymph node metastasis of gastric cancer.
journal_articles.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with a strong propensity for lymph node metastasis. To characterize the metastatic ecosystem, we perform integrated single-cell transcriptomic and T cell receptor profiling of 156,871 cells from 30 primary tumors and matched sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs), spanning non-metastatic and metastatic tumors and SLNs from non-metastatic to micro- and macro-metastatic states. We identify LN-enriched progenitor exhausted T cells as a potential reservoir for tumor-infiltrating exhausted CD8+ T cells and reveal dynamic remodeling of the lymph node microenvironment by tumor-associated macrophages during disease progression. We further show that ILC3s promote a pro-metastatic microenvironment in micro-metastatic lymph nodes through the AREG-EGFR axis, facilitating lymphatic dissemination and subsequent establishment of CD24+ tumor cells. Collectively, these findings provide a stage-resolved view of the tumor-lymph node metastatic ecosystem and identify potential therapeutic targets in GC.

journal_articles.title: The TCF-1-E-protein axis preserves stem-like Th17 identity and prevents autoimmune pathology.
journal_articles.abstract: T helper 17 (Th17) cells exhibit plasticity, transitioning from homeostatic cells to pathogenic effectors in autoimmune diseases. Although TCF-1 restrains Th17 pathogenicity by binding RORγt, mechanisms sustaining TCF-1 expression in mature Th17 cells and the transcriptional architecture governing the switch between states remain unknown. Using an interleukin 17 (IL-17) fate-mapping system deleting Tcf7 in cells with IL-17 history, we show that TCF-1 maintains homeostatic Th17 identity. TCF-1 deficiency does not impair Th17 generation but destabilizes the non-pathogenic state, causing loss of stem-like markers (SLAMF6 and CD27), acquisition of pathogenic features (CXCR6, T-bet, and IFN-γ), and exacerbated experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis. Mechanistically, TCF-1 and E-proteins form a reciprocal feedback loop establishing a self-reinforcing transcriptional circuit; disruption of either collapses this circuit and unleashes pathogenicity. Single-cell transcriptomics reveals that TCF-1 downregulation is an early event in pathogenic conversion. Thus, the TCF-1-E-protein axis sustains TCF-1 expression and prevents pathogenic conversion.

journal_articles.title: Vcam1 in endothelial and stromal cells regulates hematopoietic stem cell contact with the niche.
journal_articles.abstract: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) are essential for differentiation into all blood cell types. In mammals, the interaction between HSPCs and the fetal liver niche during development is critical for stem cell maturation. Integrin alpha 4 (Itga4) on HSPCs and vascular cell adhesion molecule (Vcam1) on niche cells are critical for HSPC colonization of the fetal liver (FL). Itga4 and Vcam1 also function in the zebrafish equivalent of the FL, the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT), however, the specific niche cells that express Vcam1 remain unclear. Using multiple approaches, including fluorescent in situ hybridization, we found Vcam1 is expressed in endothelial cells (ECs) and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), but not macrophages. Time-lapse live imaging of itga4 mutants showed the Itga4-Vcam1 axis is not required for guiding HSPCs into the CHT niche but is required for their retention. Our results show that Itga4 on HSPCs, and Vcam1 on ECs and MSCs, are involved in CHT niche retention.

journal_articles.title: CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits.
journal_articles.abstract: Astrocytes perform a diverse range of tasks that facilitate brain physiology, raising the possibility that these diverse astrocytic roles are enabled by functionally distinct subtypes1,2. Recent studies identified molecular diversity among astrocytes3; however, whether this molecular heterogeneity reflects specialized astrocyte subpopulations with distinct functions remains unclear. Here, on the basis of previous molecular and functional studies4, we generated a CD51-FLP mouse line that enables direct comparison of the functional properties between CD51+ and CD51- astrocyte subpopulations in neural circuits in vivo. We show that CD51+ and CD51- astrocytes have unique morphological, physiological and developmental properties in both the cortex and hippocampus. Functional studies demonstrate that CD51+ astrocytes selectively promote synapse formation in the developing cortex and circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, we found that CD51+ astrocytes function through glypican 6 to promote synapse formation in the cortex, while CD51 itself drives circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Applying these findings to brain injury, we found that CD51+ astrocytes promote functional recovery after stroke through enhanced synaptic remodelling. Taken together, our studies identify specialized astrocyte subpopulations that exhibit distinct functional properties in the developing, mature and injured brain.

journal_articles.title: Persistent neuronal stress signalling underlies Angelman syndrome phenotypes.
journal_articles.abstract: Angelman syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by the loss of UBE3A, a gene that encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase1,2. The mechanisms that underlie Angelman syndrome are not well understood, and in particular, the link between UBE3A substrates and disease phenotypes remains uncertain3. Here, using gain- and loss-of-function mutations in UBE3A4,5 along with unbiased proteomics, we show that asparagine synthetase (ASNS) is a target of UBE3A. We find that ASNS protein abundance is increased in the brains of Ube3a-null mice and in human neurons6. Genetic correction of ASNS overabundance rescues microcephaly and many behavioural deficits. Detailed molecular analyses show that ASNS overabundance activates stress signalling and causes a global reduction in neuronal protein synthesis. Our results suggest that loss of UBE3A traps neurons in a state of persistent stress and stunts neuronal growth during developmentally sensitive periods. Moreover, our results indicate that targeting ASNS and the stress response could hold therapeutic potential in Angelman syndrome.

journal_articles.title: Programmable design of functional proteins from natural language.
journal_articles.abstract: Programming biological function-designing bespoke proteins to perform specified molecular tasks-is a foundational goal of molecular engineering. However, current design models remain fundamentally limited1-3: they typically require either natural proteins as starting points for optimization or manual reformulation of functional goals as geometric and sequence-level constraints to guide candidate generation. Here we introduce Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter foundation model that designs candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function. Trained on 1.7 billion synthetically annotated protein-text pairs, Pinal links functional intent to protein sequence and structure. In computational evaluations, generated candidates combined high predicted foldability with functional-description alignment and sequence diversity, providing a basis for prioritizing experimentally testable designs. We applied Pinal to four distinct design tasks-a fluorescent protein, a polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase, an alcohol dehydrogenase and a metabolic H-protein-and experimentally observed the intended function in each case, including catalytic activity for both designed enzymes. Without iterative experimental optimization, a Pinal-designed H-protein increased product titre by 1.7-fold relative to the corresponding native Escherichia coli H-protein in a multi-enzyme CO2 fixation pathway. These findings support natural language as a high-level interface for candidate generation in protein design, enabling programmable exploration with reduced reliance on manually specified structural or sequence constraints.

journal_articles.title: The anatomy of a personal health agent.
journal_articles.abstract: Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored1,2. Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly.

journal_articles.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing.
journal_articles.abstract: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization.

journal_articles.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

journal_articles.title: A multifunctional PKS-NRPS megasynthetase in nematodes produces divergent signaling molecules that control different developmental arrests.
journal_articles.abstract: To maximize their reproductive success, nematodes not only must arrest their development in response to adverse growth conditions but also must quickly recover if conditions improve. However, the molecular signals that coordinate these transitions remain poorly understood. Here, we show that a hybrid polyketide synthase (PKS)-nonribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) expressed in the canal-associated neurons (CANs) is a central regulator of multiple developmental arrest programs, including starvation-induced larval arrest and dauer development. Using unbiased, comparative metabolomics in the predatory nematode Pristionchus pacificus, we show that this PKS-NRPS assembly line produces a suite of secondary metabolites, including a family of hybrid polyketide-nonribosomal peptides known as the nemamides, the related nemaketides, and a family of ascarylose-modified polyketides that we term ascarenes. Depending on the starter unit that is loaded onto the assembly line, the PKS-NRPS megasynthetase can produce dramatically different downstream products. Genetic analysis of the assembly line suggests that the nemamides promote recovery from starvation-induced larval arrest, while the ascarenes inhibit dauer development. Our work demonstrates that the PKS-NRPS assembly line serves as a signaling hub in the CANs, producing multiple signaling molecules that control different developmental events.

journal_articles.title: Characterization of hypothetical proteins reveals function modules and virulence factors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
journal_articles.abstract: Hypothetical proteins (HPs), known as biological dark matter, are genetic sequences of which the biological functions and regulatory processes remain largely unclear. In Pseudomonas aeruginosa, HPs account for 36.4% of all coding genes, representing a significant gap in understanding their functions and contribution to the virulence network. To address these challenges, we present a deletion repertoire comprising 938 strains targeting 1165 HPs in P. aeruginosa. Starting with transcriptome-wide analysis, we inferred putative functional predictions for HP mutants through systematic profiling of differential expression and candidate transcriptional pathways. We integrated our expression profiles with public datasets (5707 genes × 2312 conditions). This allowed us to distinguish constitutively expressed genes from variable genes. Using independent component analysis (ICA), we identified 56 independent regulatory Modules, providing a comprehensive transcriptional-association framework. These contributed to the discovery and experimental validation of 20 virulence-related hypothetical proteins (VRHPs) and 3 antibiotic resistance-related hypothetical proteins (ARHPs). Evolutionary analysis across bacterial taxa provided additional insights into HP sequence conservation and evolutionary dynamics. In summary, our study presents a large-scale HP mutant library combined with integrated transcriptomic and machine learning approaches, establishing both a valuable resource and a systematic strategy for predicting and prioritizing candidate functions of HPs across bacterial species.

journal_articles.title: Cross-talk of filter gate and lower helices drives polymodal regulation and disease in TREK channels.
journal_articles.abstract: The TREK two-pore domain potassium channels regulate membrane excitability and respond to diverse physiological stimuli. Single-site mutations of TREK are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders and can cause pathological channel hyperactivation. Here, using the OneOPES enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics framework, we characterize the energetics of conformational transition along a predefined pathway connecting the up and down states of TREK-2, together with initial conformational rearrangements of the selectivity filter under physiological stimuli and disease-mimicking conditions. The simulations reveal a shared energetic axis coupling the lower helices, proximal C-terminus, and selectivity filter to govern channel gating. Predicted conformational effects of a disease-mimicking mutation were validated electrophysiologically using a conformation-sensitive TREK-2 inhibitor. Together with our previous unbiased MD simulations, these results establish an energetic framework for TREK-2 regulation and dysfunction, complementing prior structural and mechanistic studies while highlighting the potential and methodological challenges of advanced enhanced-sampling approaches for resolving complex conformational landscapes of ion channels.
