journal_articles.title: Optogenetic reduction of theta oscillations induces remapping of time cells without memory impairment.
journal_articles.abstract: In a delayed alternation spatial working memory task, hippocampal time cells fire during specific moments of the delay period to form a sequential representation of the entire delay interval. The causal relationship between these sequences and working memory remains unclear. Similarly, hippocampal theta oscillations are thought to support working memory, primarily through the generation of time cell sequences. To causally examine these relationships, we optogenetically silence the medial septal GABAergic theta-generating circuit during the delay portion of a delayed spatial alternation task. With hippocampal theta oscillations substantially reduced, many time cells exhibit remapping, and new time cells are recruited. Despite partial remapping of time cell sequences, behavioral performance remains intact and trajectory-specific coding is preserved, suggesting that task-relevant information remains available under theta disruption.

journal_articles.title: Organization of retrosplenial cortex projections at the single-neuron level.
journal_articles.abstract: The retrosplenial cortex (RSP) supports spatial cognition, memory, and brain-wide information integration, yet its output architecture remains poorly resolved at single-neuron resolution. Using fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography (fMOST), we reconstruct sparsely labeled neurons sampled predominantly from the anterior RSP across the whole brain. We find three major projection routes-cortical-restricted (CR), thalamic-restricted (TR), and thalamic-brainstem collateral (TBC)-and classify neurons into ten projection subtypes with distinct target-selective profiles. Somatic location and volumetric features are associated with axonal projection patterns. TR-pattern neurons show subregion-dependent thalamic targeting, whereas TBC-pattern neurons display greater axonal complexity and subtype-specific collateralization toward thalamic, midbrain, and hindbrain targets. Bilaterally projecting neurons across distinct projection patterns show cross-network projection modes with an overall ipsilateral preference and laminar-specific commissural architectures. Together, these findings provide a single-neuron anatomical map of RSP cortical, thalamic, and cortico-subcortical output patterns and a framework for examining distributed information processing across brain-wide networks.

journal_articles.title: Polycystin-2 functions as a calcium leak channel under endoplasmic reticulum stress to protect against myocardial ischemia.
journal_articles.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress activates the unfolded protein response (UPR) to enhance metabolism and restore homeostasis by increasing mitochondrial calcium at mitochondrial-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites (MERCs). Unresolved ER stress is deleterious and contributes to the severity of diseases such as myocardial infarction (MI). The identity of the MERC calcium source and its interplay with the UPR is unclear. We find that ER-localized polycystin-2 (PC2), a calcium channel, is upregulated in cardiomyocytes with MI. Cardiomyocyte PC2-knockout mice with MI exhibit worsened heart function and decreased PERK. ER stress induces a PC2-facilitated adaptive ER calcium leak and PC2 localization to MERCs. PC2 requires PERK phosphorylation for mitochondrial calcium transfer. PC2 mutations impair ER calcium leak, restored by full-length PC2 expression. Thus, PC2 functions in a PERK-dependent manner under ER stress to provide mitochondrial calcium, and its upregulation is cardioprotective in MI.

journal_articles.title: The COX2-PGE2-PKA axis suppresses antiviral immunity by inhibiting mtDNA-dependent STING activation.
journal_articles.abstract: The stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway is essential for mounting robust innate immunity, yet its chronic activation can drive detrimental inflammation. Although multiple cell-autonomous mechanisms that restrain STING signaling have been reported, whether inflammatory mediators within the tissue microenvironment regulate STING activation remains elusive. Using herpes simplex virus type 1 infection as a model of STING activation, we revealed that the COX2-PGE2-PKA axis functions as a critical negative regulator of STING-mediated antiviral innate immunity. Mechanistically, PGE2 acts through the EP4-PKA cascade to induce PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)-mediated mitophagy by phosphorylating STOML2 at Ser29. This pathway facilitates the clearance of damaged mitochondria that serve as a source of immunostimulatory cytosolic mitochondrial DNA, thereby attenuating downstream STING activation and type I interferons while promoting viral replication. Together, these findings establish mitochondrial quality control as the mechanistic link between PGE2 signaling and mtDNA-dependent STING activation and identify the COX2-PGE2-PKA pathway as a druggable therapeutic target to enhance STING-mediated innate immunity.

journal_articles.title: The conserved NUS-1/DHDDS-1 complex links N-glycosylation to lipid and lysosomal homeostasis in C. elegans.
journal_articles.abstract: N-glycosylation is essential for proteome integrity, yet the systemic roles of the cis-prenyltransferase (cis-PT) complex remain poorly defined. Using Caenorhabditis elegans, we demonstrate that this complex is a dual regulator of global lipid and lysosomal homeostasis. Mechanistically, NUS-1 physically associates with the core oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) complex to coordinate N-glycan transfer. Loss of NUS-1/DHDDS-1 triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, lysosomal collapse, and systemic lipopenia. This lipid defect arises from impaired N-glycosylation of the SREBP cleavage-activating protein (SCAP). cis-PT deficiency causes unglycosylated SCAP to undergo massive degradation and absolute physical entrapment within the ER, preventing SREBP nuclear translocation and downstream lipid synthesis. Furthermore, pathogenic mutations cause dysfunction through distinct molecular mechanisms: pocket integrity disruption or catalytic impairment. These findings uncover an essential crosstalk between protein glycosylation and global lipid metabolism, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding the systemic pathophysiology of congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG).

journal_articles.title: The lysis mechanism of the haloarchaeal virus HFTV1.
journal_articles.abstract: Tailed bacteriophages can lyse their host with help of the holin-endolysin system. However, for archaeal tailed viruses (arTVs), whose archaeal hosts have a fundamentally different cell envelope, lysis mechanisms are unknown. In this study, we use the model archaeal virus-host system: Haloferax tailed virus 1 (HFTV1), which infects the methanobacteriote Haloferax gibbonsii LR2-5. We identified and characterized the lysis protein GP33, a small membrane protein that has no sequence homology with bacterial holins. Overexpression resulted in cell lysis, and the protein forms foci near the cell envelope. Molecular dynamics simulation suggests that it forms pores from which the lipids are repelled, which might result in cell lysis. Indeed, atomic force microscopy (AFM) showed that GP33 forms pores in membranes, which lead to complete membrane disruption at higher concentrations. With this work, we gain insight into a lysis mechanism from a tailed archaeal virus at the molecular level.

journal_articles.title: A single archaeon couples long-chain fatty acid oxidation to methanogenesis.
journal_articles.abstract: Anaerobic degradation of complex organic compounds to methane and carbon dioxide is common in the deep subsurface biosphere and has long been considered to require syntrophic cooperation, with methanogens confined to the terminal use of simple C1 and C2 substrates. Thermodynamic considerations, multi-omics analyses and microcosm experiments suggest that archaeal lineages are capable of methanogenic degradation of complex substrates1-6. However, experimental validation in pure culture was lacking. Here we report the isolation of a thermophilic archaeon, Methanoglobus dolicholipophagus AA-75, affiliated with Archaeoglobi, from a Chinese petroleum reservoir. Strain AA-75 not only converts methanol into methane, carbon dioxide and acetate, but also uses saturated fatty acids varying from C7:0 to C18:0 and unsaturated fatty acids including C16:1, C18:1 and C18:2 to produce methane. We term the latter lipotrophic methanogenesis, which integrates β-oxidation of fatty acids with the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway and the canonical methyl-tetrahydromethanopterin:coenzyme M methyltransferase and methyl-coenzyme M reductase complexes, together with an intracellular electron transfer system. A formaldehyde-methanol branch probably functions as an auxiliary route for C1 metabolism during methanogenesis. Methane produced from stearate is moderately 13C-enriched (δ13C-CH4 = -40.0‰ to -36.3‰), distinct from the strong 13C depletion characteristic of canonical methanogenic pathways. These findings demonstrate that methanogens can function as primary degraders of complex organic matter, challenging the classical syntrophic paradigm and calling for refinement of current models of carbon cycling in the deep subsurface biosphere.

journal_articles.title: Additive manufacturing of ultralong and architected single crystals.
journal_articles.abstract: Single-crystal materials are indispensable for high-performance applications, yet their deployment remains constrained by conventional manufacturing techniques that depend on strict quasi-steady thermal conditions1. This requirement fundamentally conflicts with the intense cyclic thermal fluctuations inherent to additive manufacturing2, historically preventing the 3D printing of large or architected single crystals. Here we present a free-form additive manufacturing approach that resolves this contradiction by using delicately controlled alternating and pulsed heat inputs to govern and direct single-crystal growth. Using this method, we demonstrate the fabrication of metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V alongside, to our knowledge, the first single-crystal lattice structures containing complex zigzag ligaments, effectively eliminating theoretical size constraints for single-crystal components. The resulting bulk single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V exhibits an order-of-magnitude increase in creep resistance over standard grain-size scaling predictions, driven by the synergistic elimination of grain boundaries and an additive manufacturing-induced hierarchical α/β-architecture that regulates dislocation density, mobility and void evolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate the broad applicability of this technique by printing single crystals of hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys. Our work introduces a large-scale method for single-crystal additive manufacturing, expanding the accessible materials library and enabling high-performance, complex geometries previously unattainable by classical methods.

journal_articles.title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts.
journal_articles.abstract: The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation1-5, rising tree mortality6-8 and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest9-11. Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions1-4,11,12. Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable1,9,13. Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts9,14-17. Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO2 measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr-1, with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr-1) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011-2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr-1) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019-2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr-1) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr-1) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning.

journal_articles.title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis.
journal_articles.abstract: Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species1-3, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans. Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2-BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington's disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

journal_articles.title: Cortex-wide imaging in naturally behaving mice with 1-gram wireless mesoscopes.
journal_articles.abstract: Revealing how distributed cortical circuits coordinate behavior in freely moving animals remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience, constrained by limited fields of view, low throughput, and the tethering required by current miniaturized microscopes1-4. Here, we present Airscope, a wireless mesoscope delivering 4 μm lateral resolution across a 6 mm field of view at 12.5 Hz, weighing 1.0 gram. An aspheric-lens design achieves a 2.84× shorter total track length than previous miniaturized microscopes1,2,5,6 while matching the neuron yield of benchtop one-photon mesoscopes; a tailored wireless link supports cable-free calcium imaging from >8,500 neurons per animal (25‑fold increase). Paired with a zero-shot behavior analyzer, Airscope enables cortical imaging across rich behavioral conditions, including room-scale enriched arenas, swimming assays, and multi-organ implantation, with concurrent recording from multiple animals. Using Airscope, we demonstrate versatile applications of untethered cortical imaging across diverse behavioral paradigms. We identify cortical activity patterns across multiple dorsal regions that correlate with behavioral signatures of social dominance, and show dorsal-cortical population activity prospectively decodes competition outcomes across paired animals. We observe reward-location-associated cortical activity patterns during maze exploration, and characterize Granger-causal influence from spinal cord to cortex during fear conditioning, enabled by simultaneous brain-spinal recordings. By uniting large-scale, cellular-resolution recording with unconstrained behavior, Airscope makes naturalistic, multi-animal cortical recording experimentally practical, and provides a broadly accessible technology for systems neuroscience.

journal_articles.title: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts.
journal_articles.abstract: The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins.1-5 This challenge is acute for metal polypyridine photocatalysts, which are widely used in visible-light chemistry but have not enabled highly enantioselective photocatalysis within protein scaffolds. In this study, we show that generative protein design6-8 can create de novo scaffolds that selectively bind these photocatalysts and that directed evolution converts the resulting artificial metalloenzymes into efficient, highly enantioselective photocatalysts9. The evolved proteins support diverse light-driven reactions, high catalyst turnover and catalyst recycling, and can function with commercially available racemic metal complexes. Spectroscopic studies show that the protein environment extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity. These findings establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds for synthetic metal complexes that lack natural protein partners and provide a strategy for combining protein design and evolution to control non-natural catalytic chemistry.

journal_articles.title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators.
journal_articles.abstract: Interactions among species are increasingly recognized as key determinants of climate change impacts on ecosystems1-5. However, we know little about how climatic perturbations affect interactions among top vertebrate predators. Here we show that, when an emergent disease caused the decline of shared prey (rabbits), after decades of neutral co-existence a mammalian carnivore (lynx) started to prey heavily on a top predatory raptor (kites). These predation bouts occurred exclusively under drought conditions and when lynx found rabbit remains under the raptor nests, consistent with the removal of a potential competitor. Drought-induced lynx predation depressed lifetime reproductive success and triggered territory abandonment and dispersal by the raptor, suggestive of a new arms race among predators. A reduction in raptor abundance was associated with an increase in an insectivorous bird (a small owl), showing that the new interaction had the potential to reach lower trophic levels. These results underline the importance of diet flexibility and mobility as important mediators of resilience to stressors. In the future, synergistic effects of multiple anthropogenic stressors may reshape the interactions and ecological roles of many apex predators, with potential cascading consequences for whole ecosystems. A key to forecasting the future impact of global change may reside in understanding how behavioural flexibility and interacting keystone species respond to interacting shocks.

journal_articles.title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea.
journal_articles.abstract: The accumulation of persistent plastics in the ocean is causing wide-ranging environmental problems1-3. Some commercially available compostable plastics4-7, developed to address these issues, degrade efficiently under industrial composting conditions; however, their degradation in marine environments, particularly in the deep sea, remains limited8-10. Here we demonstrate that thermally embedding enzymes into compostable polyesters (poly(butylene succinate) (PBS), poly(butylene succinate-co-adipate) (PBSA), poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT)) significantly accelerates their degradation in both coastal and deep-sea environments from water depths of 2-6 m to 5,503 m. Enzyme-embedded polyesters achieved near-complete degradation at a deep-sea depth of 757 m within 5 months. Furthermore, moderate biodegradation of enzyme-embedded polyesters was observed under extreme conditions on deep-sea floors of 5,503 m. In coastal seawater, films embedded with trace amounts (0.1 wt%) of enzyme underwent rapid degradation. The mechanical properties of enzyme-embedded polyesters were similar to those of enzyme-free polyesters. Chemical analysis confirmed the formation of low-molecular-mass degradation products and biochemical oxygen demand measurements supported the mineralization of the enzyme-embedded polyesters. The enzyme-embedding strategy enables enhanced marine degradation of compostable polyesters and represents a potential solution to marine plastic pollution.

journal_articles.title: Functional architecture of the human insula.
journal_articles.abstract: The insular cortex has a central role in pain1,2, interoception3,4 and feelings5,6, yet its functional architecture and causal electrophysiological relationships among its subregions remain poorly understood. Here we combine intracranial electrical stimulation and task-based electroencephalography recordings with connectivity mapping within a cytoarchitectonic atlas of the human insula7-10 in 87 participants implanted with intracranial electrodes, and identify a quadripartite functional architecture comprising four distinct regions: (1) a dorsal-posterior region encoding somatotopically organized nociceptive/thermoceptive and somatosensory signals; (2) a ventral-posterior region with access to somatic information across multiple body parts; (3) a mid-anterior region associated with visceral sensations and anxiety states; and (4) an anterior-polar region, largely silent to direct stimulation, yet showing robust activation during salience detection and change of action mode. Critically, this anterior region, with its strong connections with the prefrontal cortex, including the anterior cingulate cortex, exerts strong and direct influence over other insular regions, while receiving less-strong indirect inputs from them, revealing an electrophysiological pathway for cognitive modulation of pain and bodily perception. Together, these findings define a functional architecture of the human insula that links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

journal_articles.title: GRP75-dependent SIMPA mediates inter-organellar quality control.
journal_articles.abstract: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress1. Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health2-7. However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light-electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness.

journal_articles.title: Multimodal precision diagnostics in clinical xenotransplantation.
journal_articles.abstract: Recent breakthroughs in pig-to-human xenotransplantation have successfully prevented hyperacute rejection of kidney, heart, liver and lung xenografts, marking a milestone long considered a critical barrier. However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date. Detection and management of these injuries remain a critical bottleneck, as conventional histopathology and standard clinical monitoring lack the sensitivity required to identify subclinical injury early enough to guide timely intervention. This diagnostic gap underscores an urgent need for the development of advanced, multimodal precision diagnostic frameworks to enhance immune surveillance, which will be essential for standardizing clinical protocols and enabling pathogenesis-driven therapeutic intervention. This approach will inform both immunosuppressive regimens and future gene editing strategies aimed at engineering rejection-resistant porcine organs, ultimately prolonging graft survival. Broad adoption of such an integrative strategy will be essential to transition xenotransplantation from an experimental intervention into a safe, scalable and patient-centred clinical therapy. In this Review, we synthesize recent progress in xenotransplantation and position multimodal precision diagnostics as a pivotal strategy to address the remaining immunological and clinical barriers to widespread clinical implementation.

journal_articles.title: Octupole-driven spin torque switching of antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions.
journal_articles.abstract: Magnetic tunnel junctions based on ferromagnets are canonical devices in spintronics, with wide-ranging applications in data storage, computing and sensing. They simultaneously exhibit mechanisms for electrical detection and control of magnetic order through the tunnelling magnetoresistance (TMR)1-5 and spin-transfer torque6-9 effects, respectively. It was long assumed that neither of these effects could be sizeable in all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions (AATJs), considering that they have no net magnetization. However, it was recently shown that AATJs based on chiral antiferromagnets do exhibit TMR due to their non-relativistic momentum-dependent spin polarization and cluster magnetic octupole moment, which are manifestations of their spin-split band structure10-13. However, the reciprocal effect, that is, the antiferromagnetic counterpart of spin-transfer torque, has been assumed non-existent due to the total electric current being spin-neutral. Here we report nanoscale AATJs that display this reciprocal effect, which we term octupole-driven spin-transfer torque (OTT). We demonstrate current-induced OTT switching of PtMn3|MgO|PtMn3 AATJs, with a TMR value of 363% at room temperature and switching current densities of the order of 10 MA cm-2. Our theoretical modelling explains the origin of OTT in terms of the imbalance between intra- and inter-sublattice spin currents across the AATJ, and, equivalently, in terms of the non-zero net cluster octupole polarization of each PtMn3 layer. This work establishes a new materials platform for antiferromagnetic spintronics and provides a pathway towards deeply scaled magnetic memory and room-temperature terahertz technologies.

journal_articles.title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses.
journal_articles.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells1. However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms-occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus-receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike.

journal_articles.title: The contribution of salt marshes to wave attenuation during extreme storms.
journal_articles.abstract: Salt marshes protect coastlines by attenuating wind waves with their elevated marsh platform and above-ground vegetation1. Confidence in the persistence of this service under a changing climate requires knowledge on how extreme storms damage the platform and vegetation; however, a comprehensive, quantified understanding of salt marsh-wave interactions under extreme events is lacking. A unique experiment was conducted by transferring intact salt marsh to one of the world's largest wave flumes, and subsequently exposing it to increasingly higher waves that reach up to 2 m significant wave height. We show that marsh substrates can persist with negligible erosion, despite cumulative wave exposure. By contrast, the vegetation was progressively damaged during continued wave exposure, gradually reducing vegetation-related wave attenuation. Results emphasize that vegetation was most effective in attenuating waves at low-energy marsh coasts (up to 1 m), where attenuation exceeded 10% (up to 50%), whereas attenuation at high-energy marsh coasts (wave height > 1 m) does not exceed 10%. Our global assessment supports the differentiation between low- and high-energetic conditions resulting from the flume experiment. Our results suggest that the marsh platform remains stable under extreme wave events and that substantial wave attenuation by marsh vegetation is limited to low-energy marsh coasts.

journal_articles.title: The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology.
journal_articles.abstract: The taxonomy and phylogeny of late Middle Pleistocene hominins in East Asia remain highly debated1. Xujiayao, a key representative assemblage with many fossils and a clear stratigraphy dating to around 199-138 thousand years ago, has been extensively studied, but its evolutionary position remains uncertain. Here, to clarify this, we analysed Xujiayao material through both palaeoproteomic analysis and morphological comparisons with other East Asian late Middle Pleistocene archaic Homo. Proteomic analysis of two specimens identified 18 endogenous proteins, and the Denisova-specific COL1A2-996 R>K mutation strongly supported their affiliation with the Denisovan lineage. Extended analysis identifies a set of shared morphological traits between Denisovan fossils (Xujiayao and Harbin) and other East Asian late Middle Pleistocene archaic Homo (such as Jinniushan, Dali and Hualongdong), indicating that they all belong to the Denisovan lineage. This analysis provides a comprehensive view of Denisovan features, showing both traits reminiscent of Homo erectus (such as a thick cranial vault) and those characteristic of modern humans (for example, a strongly arched temporal squama). They also share features with late Neanderthals, such as the structure of the temporal labyrinth and the presence of a suprainiac fossa. Notably, Denisovans are distinctive, with a low cranial profile with near-parallel lateral walls, a massive supraorbital torus, a flat zygomaxillary region and weak prognathism.

journal_articles.title: Touch-sensing digital pixel fibre enables interactive garment GUI.
journal_articles.abstract: Wearable computing promises to transform human interaction with information, yet conventional graphical user interfaces (GUIs) rely on planar, rigid displays incompatible with textiles, which are composed of one-dimensional fibres. Despite recent progress1,2 in flexible and fibre-based displays, bridging this fundamental dimensional mismatch remains challenging because existing approaches do not naturally provide the digitally addressable, high-throughput, information-rich interfaces required for interactive GUIs. Here we present a digital pixel fibre integrating addressable pixels, a common propagation-axis interconnection for scalable in-fibre circuitry and a coaxial sensing layer for fibre-level touch localization. Microelectronic components and a touch-gated resistive path system form a linear circuit that acts as both an interactive display backbone and a computational bus, while peripheral multimodal fibre sensors and actuators enable physiological, inertial, optical, and acoustic input and output. We integrate these fibres into the forearm portion of a garment sleeve to realize a GUI with a 96 × 54-pixel display, 30-frame-per-second refresh rate and 8-bit colour depth. It supports dynamic graphics, integrated audio-video playback, wireless data exchange and interactive computing functions, while maintaining the flexibility, washability, breathability and mechanical robustness of everyday textiles. By merging display, sensing and computation within a single fibre, this work establishes a scalable platform for intrinsically interactive textiles, opening pathways toward garments that operate as fully integrated computational systems.

journal_articles.title: WEE1 opposes APC/CCDH1 activity to promote S phase entry.
journal_articles.abstract: WEE1 phosphorylates and inhibits the activity of cyclin-dependent kinases to prevent mitotic entry and establish a G2 DNA damage checkpoint1-3. Consequently, WEE1 inhibitors have been developed to be synthetically lethal in TP53-mutated tumours that become reliant on this WEE1-mediated checkpoint, and such inhibitors are undergoing clinical trials. However, WEE1 inhibitors also have efficacy in TP53-wild-type tumours, and many trials have been terminated owing to high levels of toxic side effects, suggesting that WEE1 has unknown functions. Here we show that WEE1 promotes cell cycle re-entry from quiescence (G0) by opposing the activity of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome bound to CDH1 (APC/CCDH1). WEE1 phosphorylates CDH1 (FZR1) at key residues that mediate the interaction between CDH1 and APC/C. Cells with loss of function of WEE1 during G0/G1 have delayed S phase entry, impaired G1/S transition, abnormal S phase accumulation of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21Cip1/Kip1 and a p21-dependent G2 arrest. Reduced expression of APC/CCDH1 or p21 renders cells more sensitive to acute WEE1 inhibition, and both pathways are downregulated in cells with acquired WEE1 inhibitor resistance. These results reveal a mechanism of cell cycle control that has implications for how WEE1 inhibitors should be used in the clinic.

journal_articles.title: Zeolite-catalysed olefin carbonylation based on tuning spatial confinement.
journal_articles.abstract: Carbonylation is an important process used to produce aldehydes, carboxylic acids and esters1-5 that is usually catalysed by homogeneous metal complexes with ligands and iodide promoters6-12. Koch has reported that protons of mineral acids can also catalyse carbonylation13. Previous studies have demonstrated that Brønsted acidic zeolites can act as a heterogeneous, Koch-type catalyst for carbonylation of alcohols and olefins, but the products in this case are limited to tertiary carboxylic acids14-18. Here we show that targeted use of spatial confinement in a zeolite together with a high CO/olefin ratio can help break this limitation. We report that, with FER zeolite and a CO/olefin ratio of 360, olefin carbonylation can produce primary and secondary carboxylic acids as the main products; ethylene carbonylation to propanoic acid (PA) is achieved with 80% selectivity over 100 h and propylene carbonylation to isobutyric acid (IBA) is achieved with 95% selectivity over 750 h. The propylene and ethylene carbonylation selectivities decrease to 61% and 57%, respectively, as the CO/olefin ratio decreases to 24 and 90, respectively. Experiments in combination with theoretical calculations suggest that T2-O5 in eight-membered ring (8-MR) cavities of FER zeolite are the primary active sites for ethylene carbonylation and T3-O1 in ten-membered rings (10-MRs) are the primary active sites for propylene carbonylation. Our findings open new directions for olefin carbonylation and provide critical insights into the prerequisites for developing new zeolite-based carbonylation processes.

journal_articles.title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity.
journal_articles.abstract: Microorganisms have the potential to deliver growth-promoting benefits to plants and crops; however, to be useful in a field setting, their gene expression should be programmable and restricted to specific plant hosts and conditions. Here, using O-methyl-L-tyrosine (OMY) as a model compound, we establish noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a tool for plant-based control of associated microbial activity. We use genetic code expansion to engineer OMY-dependent control of protein synthesis in the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis. Engineered B. subtilis strains express an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pair that, upon provision of OMY, results in suppression of in-frame amber stop codons in target transcripts. We engineer Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to biosynthesize OMY, showing that plant-derived OMY can stimulate gene expression in both model and wild soil bacteria. This demonstrates that inducible and tissue-specific expression of a single biosynthetic enzyme by the plant enables on-demand control over microbial activity, establishing ncAAs as a tool for programming plant-microorganism partnerships.

journal_articles.title: Structural variant detection across sequencing technologies.
journal_articles.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are a major source of genomic diversity, yet their discovery remains challenging due to repetitive genomic contexts, alignment ambiguity and the trade-off between sequencing cost and read length. Here we introduce HitSV, which implements repetitiveness- and signature-density-aware breakpoint recognition coupled with precise haplotype-resolved local assembly, thereby enabling base-resolution SV reconstruction and genotyping in various sequencing technologies. On the HG002 benchmark, HitSV achieved 15-72% (long read), 10-36% (short read) and 12% (hybrid sequencing), respectively, higher genotype F1 scores than state-of-the-art SV callers. Applied to the 1KGP phase 4 cohort, HitSV expanded the SV callset by 31.5%, substantially reshaping allele-frequency landscapes. In a large Chinese long-read cohort, HitSV uncovered tandem-repeat-mobile-element composite arrays as a prevalent, multi-allelic class of complex SVs, highlighting composite repeat architectures as an important and previously underrecognized contributor to human structural variation.

journal_articles.title: Monocyte surface Y RNAs potentiate innate immunity.
journal_articles.abstract: RNAs can associate with the surface of diverse cell types, yet the functions of specific RNA species on primary immune cells remain unclear. Here, utilizing methods developed to profile, image and quantify surface RNAs in rare primary cell populations, we found that Y RNAs, a family of small noncoding RNAs, preferentially localize to human monocyte surface. In an exploratory pooled inflammatory bowel disease cohort, the proportion of cell-surface-Y-RNA-positive peripheral monocytes was markedly higher in patients with inflammatory bowel disease than in healthy donors or individuals with irritable bowel syndrome. In vivo depletion of cell-surface Y RNAs ameliorates disease activity in mice with colitis. Mechanistically, cell-surface Y RNAs co-cluster with Toll-like receptors TLR2 and TLR4, bind extracellular histones and promote receptor-mediated histone recognition, thereby activating NF-κB and AP-1 signalling and increasing IL6 expression and IL-6 secretion. These findings identify cell-surface Y RNAs as previously unrecognized amplifiers of inflammatory activation.

journal_articles.title: The rise of reducing reagent-resistant TfR1 dimer marks ferroptosis.
journal_articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent type of cell death caused by excessive membrane lipid peroxidation. It remains a challenge to detect ferroptotic cells, especially in in vivo settings, hindering translational studies. Here we discover that a reducing reagent-resistant (3R) dimer of the transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) is a highly specific indicator for lipid peroxidation. The 3R dimer is elevated in cells when ferroptosis is induced, either by pharmacological agents or by genetic perturbations. Furthermore, the 3R dimer can be used to detect disease-associated ferroptosis in tissue and in extracellular vesicles isolated from mouse or patient plasma. Given the near-ubiquitous expression of TfR1, we posit that the 3R dimer may function as a ferroptosis marker with widespread potential utility for basic and translational studies.

journal_articles.title: 3D confinement physically regulates cell cycle progression in budding yeast.
journal_articles.abstract: Our understanding of cell division control traditionally comes via using liquid broths or 2D flat-plate cultures - which cannot recapitulate the complex visco-elasto-plastic properties of natural habitats such as tissues, mucus, and soil. Consequently, how such regimes of physical confinement influence proliferative growth remains poorly understood. Here, using engineered, mechanically tunable and transparent growth matrices, we directly visualize yeast budding and division across 3D viscoelastic regimes. We discover that elevated physical confinement drastically prolongs budding intervals without any physiological defects or activating global regulatory programs. Remarkably, extended cell division times are not associated with transcriptional or proteomic signatures of mechanosensation or cell cycle regulation. Rather, 3D confinement physically constrains the volumetric growth of incipient buds - manifesting as delayed cell cycle progression. Hence, our findings establish that physical constrainment regulates eukaryotic cell division.

journal_articles.title: A foldable small-scale soft electromagnetic robot for multimodal navigation in confined and unstructured environments.
journal_articles.abstract: Multimodal locomotion is crucial for an animal's adaptability in unstructured wild environments. Analogously, in the human gastrointestinal tract, characterized by viscoelastic mucus, complex rugae, and narrow openings like the cardia, multimodal locomotion is also essential for a small-scale soft robot to conduct tasks. Here, we introduce a small-scale, compact, foldable, and robust soft electromagnetic robot with more than nine locomotion modes designed for such a scenario. Featuring a six-spoke elastomer body embedded with liquid metal channels and driven by Laplace forces under a static magnetic field, the robot is capable of rapid transitions ( < 0.35 s) among different locomotion modes. It achieves exceptional agility, including high-speed rolling (818 mm/s, 26 body lengths per second), omnidirectional crawling, jumping, and swimming. Notably, the robot can fold to reduce its occupied volume by 79%, enabling it to traverse confined spaces. We further validate its navigation capabilities in unstructured environments, including discrete obstacles, viscoelastic gelatin surfaces, viscous fluids, 3D-printed gastric surfaces, and a porcine gastric environment. This system offers a versatile strategy for developing high-mobility soft robots for future biomedical applications.

journal_articles.title: A hypothalamic circuit links high-fat diet exposure to anxiety-like behavior and anxiety-associated hyperphagia.
journal_articles.abstract: Obesity and anxiety disorders are frequently comorbid, yet the neural circuit mechanisms linking metabolic and affective states remain incompletely understood. Here, in male mice exposed to long-term high-fat diet, we identify a hypothalamic circuit comprising arcuate nucleus agouti-related protein neurons and paraventricular nucleus corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons that regulates anxiety-like behavior under metabolic stress, with downstream recruitment of lateral hypothalamic area glutamatergic neurons to modulate feeding in a state-dependent manner. In vivo fiber photometry and ex vivo electrophysiology show that high-fat diet enhances activity and feeding-locked recruitment of this circuit, associated with increased anxiety-like behavior and feeding. Circuit-specific inhibition attenuates both phenotypes, whereas corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor 2 signaling in the lateral hypothalamic area selectively mediates high-fat diet-associated hyperphagia without affecting anxiety-like behavior. In this work, we show a disease-state-dependent hypothalamic circuit differentially recruited under chronic high-fat diet to coordinate anxiety-related behavior and feeding output, providing a framework for metabolic-affective interactions.

journal_articles.title: A lipoprotein-biomimetic nanoplatform for oncogenic KRAS mutation-specific lysosome-targeting protein degradation.
journal_articles.abstract: Lysosome-targeting protein degradation strategies have evolved to leverage lineage-specific receptors to improve selectivity, yet remain unable to distinguish malignant from normal cells within the same lineage. Since oncogenic mutations are the defining feature of malignant cells, we here develop KRAS-mutated (MT) tumor targeting chimeras (KRASTAC), a lipoprotein-biomimetic nanoplatform that hijacks the enhanced macropinocytosis in KRAS-MT cells for mutation-specific protein degradation. KRASTAC potently degrades diverse proteins including epidermal growth factor receptor and programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) in KRAS-MT cells at a low antibody concentration of 2.5 nM within 9 h, with minimal impact in KRAS wild-type (WT) cells. Furthermore, KRASTAC exhibits mutation-specific tumor accumulation and protein degradation in vivo. KRASTAC-induced PD-L1 degradation leads to robust antitumor efficacy and reprogramming of the immunosuppressive microenvironment in mice carrying Kras-MT tumors. Our work presents KRASTAC as a potent mutation-specific protein degradation strategy for KRAS-MT cancers and establishes macropinocytosis as a route for lysosome-targeting protein degradation.

journal_articles.title: A phage DUF669 protein mediates post-cleavage DNA repair against host CRISPR immunity.
journal_articles.abstract: Phages have evolved various anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins or RNA-based anti-CRISPR (Racr) to evade host CRISPR immunity by direct interference. However, whether other counter-CRISPR mechanisms exist remains unexplored. Here, we report a phage-encoded two-protein system, termed Healer, which neutralizes CRISPR immunity via a post-cleavage DNA repair mechanism. This phage replication-associated system comprises two proteins: Gp63 (a DUF669 domain-containing protein), and Gp64 (an AAA domain-containing protein). Mechanistic investigations elucidate that Gp63 acts as a rapid-response effector of CRISPR-induced DNA breaks. After Gp63 binds ssDNA, it promotes Gp64-mediated homologous recombination, which repairs CRISPR-generated phage DNA breaks and supports phage viability. Notably, co-expression of the Healer system with Cas9/Cas12 in E. coli, P. aeruginosa, and A. baumannii demonstrated high phage genome-editing efficiency. Collectively, our findings reveal an important anti-CRISPR complementary strategy, providing a promising tool for genome engineering.

journal_articles.title: A ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase facilitates H2A.Z removal in response to phosphate starvation.
journal_articles.abstract: The histone variant H2A.Z plays a critical role in the modulation of environmental responses, but the mechanisms regulating H2A.Z dynamics in response to stresses remain poorly understood in plants. Here we identify the ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase UCH2 as a Pi-responsive chromatin regulator that promotes Pi starvation-induced (PSI) gene activation. We show that PHR1 recruits UCH2 to PSI gene promoters under Pi deficiency, where UCH2 deubiquitinates H2A.Z and promotes reduction in H2A.Z occupancy at PSI gene promoters. Loss of UCH2 impairs this reduction in H2A.Z occupancy, represses PSI gene induction, and reduces Pi accumulation. A catalytically inactive UCH2 mutant fails to complement these defects, and ubiquitination-deficient H2A.Z variants render plants insensitive to UCH2 loss. Our findings establish UCH2 as a critical chromatin regulator linking Pi sensing with H2A.Z dynamics and provide insights into how plants integrate chromatin-based regulation to maintain Pi homeostasis.

journal_articles.title: Actionable genetic landscape and dynamics in circulating DNA from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer.
journal_articles.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a sensitive, noninvasive tool for monitoring the genomic landscape, heterogeneity, and evolution of cancer, aggregating genetic information from multiple metastatic sites. Here, we study 15,564 cfDNA samples from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer (MBC). We classify samples, deep-sequenced with Guardant360, into MBC subtypes using our trained random forest model. Most patients have variants associated with therapeutic resistance and targetability of approved and experimental therapies, including in PIK3CA, ESR1, PTEN, and AKT1. Frequencies of multiple actionable alterations differed from primary disease, and multiple variants per gene suggest independent resistant clones. The large cohort size enables uncovering clonal co-behaviors, including co-existence and exclusivity of alleles and correlation of allele fractions. cfDNA testing is now recommended in multiple advanced malignancies, including eligibility assessment for clinical trials. We envision this large collection of MBC cfDNA data as an invaluable resource for the design and planning of future clinical trials.

journal_articles.title: Active crustal straining and fault reactivation at Valles Marineris.
journal_articles.abstract: Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet.

journal_articles.title: Ambient, real-time digitization and datafication of glass slide microscopy towards AI-at-the-microscope.
journal_articles.abstract: Pathology remains central to clinical diagnosis, yet adoption of digital pathology is constrained by financial, operational, and workflow burdens of fully digital infrastructure. We introduce HistoCAM, a platform for ambient, real-time datafication and digitization of glass-slide microscopy that preserves microscope workflows. A 31-megapixel, high space-bandwidth-time-product camera and custom software application stream and composite the pathologist's eyepiece view, passively generating multi-resolution images from 2X to 40X while recording magnification use, search paths, and dwell times. These outputs provide immediate workflow uplift through digital annotation, measurement, quality assurance, and real-time integration of configurable AI tools. Simultaneously, HistoCAM links image content with expert interaction data and supports rapid generation of annotated, pre-embedded training data during routine slide review. By converting routine microscopy into an AI-ready data stream without requiring additional acquisition steps, HistoCAM provides a practical bridge to computational pathology while creating process-aware datasets that capture how pathologists examine and interpret tissue.

journal_articles.title: Anti-thymocyte globulin triggers TNF-dependent cell death in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
journal_articles.abstract: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) accounts for one of the most aggressive hematological tumors associated with poor prognosis, notably for relapsed and refractory patients. Hence, an unmet medical need persists for T-ALL patients who fail to durably respond to conventional treatments. Herein, we report the antileukemic efficacy of anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG), a polyclonal cocktail of IgG enriched in antibodies directed against human thymocyte antigens. The treatment of preclinical models of T-ALL reveals a cytotoxic mechanism of ATG mediated by TNFα signaling. We demonstrate that ATG resistance may occur via the induction of negative regulators of TNFα-induced cell death and can be circumvented by SMAC mimetic birinapant ex vivo and in vivo. These results are validated in a series of prospective primary relapsed/refractory T-ALL samples. Here, we provide a strong rationale for clinically relevant ATG-based immunotherapy in combination with birinapant to treat T-ALL patients.

journal_articles.title: Asymmetric basin-wide responses of coastal phytoplankton biomass to the Indian Ocean dipole.
journal_articles.abstract: Frequent Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) events exert substantial ecological pressure on marine ecosystems of the Indian Ocean. However, how coastal ecosystems respond to IOD events remains unknown. Here, combining field observations, remote sensing, and model-derived product, we reveal a basin-scale response of surface and subsurface phytoplankton along the vast eastern Indian Ocean coastline; further, the response is asymmetric between IOD phases, with a 27.0 ± 17.0% increase during positive IOD but only a 13.1 ± 5.2% decrease during negative IOD. Upwelling Kelvin waves (KWs) generated by equatorial easterly wind anomalies during positive IOD raise the thermocline and mixing intensity, increase nutrient availability, and phytoplankton biomass. In contrast, downwelling KWs generated by equatorial westerly wind anomalies during negative IOD further constrain the oligotrophy-limited phytoplankton baseline, resulting in a substantially weaker biological response. Within the KWs framework, underwater topography enhances regional sensitivity to KWs forcing, thereby amplifying the asymmetric phytoplankton biomass responses. Our findings imply that the projected increase in extreme positive IOD events will likely enhance primary production, with possible implications for regional fisheries.

journal_articles.title: Behaviorally-relevant features of observed actions dominate cortical representational geometry in natural vision.
journal_articles.abstract: We effortlessly extract behaviorally relevant information from dynamic visual input to understand the actions of others. Here, we compare behavioral judgments of action meaning against other models capturing semantic and visual features. We measured brain activity using fMRI while participants viewed 90 video clips depicting social and nonsocial actions in real-world contexts. Using arrangement tasks, we developed two behavioral models capturing judgments of action meaning (transitive purpose, social content), as well as three control models capturing judgments of visual content (people, objects, scene). We compared these models with semantic models based on word embeddings and visual models based on gaze and motion energy. Behavioral models of action meaning outperformed models of visual content, semantics, and low-level visual features across much of cortex. Transitivity and sociality captured large portions of unique variance throughout the action observation network, extending into regions not typically associated with action perception, such as ventral temporal cortex.

journal_articles.title: Biofilm formation and dynamics in the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus.
journal_articles.abstract: The picocyanobacterium Prochlorococcus is responsible for ~10% of annual marine carbon fixation and plays a role in the global carbon budget. While these phototrophs are primarily considered free-living and neutrally buoyant in the euphotic zone, we observe that they can form biofilms on diverse substrates. This trait is conserved across Prochlorococcus ecotypes, and populations continuously transition between planktonic and biofilm states via a non-genetic heritable mechanism. Throughout their growth, cells in biofilms retain a reversible, dynamic attachment state, and measurements of growth, photosynthesis, and carbon exudation rates reveal that cells in biofilms exude more organic carbon than their planktonic counterparts. Estimates of the fraction of Prochlorococcus cells attached to particles in the ocean-obtained through metagenomic analysis of serially-fractionated samples-reveal that a significant adherent population exists throughout the euphotic and mesopelagic zones. This work describes a dimension of Prochlorococcus's ecological niche and suggests a role in carbon export to the deep sea.

journal_articles.title: Bonds improve post mission disposal compliance and the sustainability of low Earth orbit.
journal_articles.abstract: Post-mission disposal (PMD) non-compliance threatens the long-term sustainability of Low Earth Orbit (LEO). Between 2010 and 2024, only 40% of satellites in non-naturally compliant orbits successfully deorbited. As launch rates and large constellations expand the active population, reducing satellite derelicts is increasingly urgent. We evaluate an escrow-based PMD performance bond that makes non-compliance financially costly while preserving access to orbit. The analysis couples an economic model of operator decision-making with a model of LEO population evolution, allowing launches and debris risk to co-evolve over 25 years. Bonds of $200,000 per satellite reduce derelict satellite mass per year by more than one-third and increase welfare by up to 27%, while bonds above $1 million show diminishing marginal returns. Even partial adoption can be effective: a bond covering 20% of the global market still improves sustainability under all levels of market leakage, although broader participation delivers greater environmental and economic benefits.

journal_articles.title: Building governance reform without accountability transfer invites urban disaster.
journal_articles.abstract: Building governance reforms can displace accountability rather than transfer it. The 2023 Türkiye earthquake disaster – in which formally inspected, post-reform buildings collapsed at scale – exemplifies this failure mode and reveals the institutional conditions required for genuine accountability transfer.

last_author.name: Cassidy Johnson
affiliations: The Bartlett Development Planning Unit, University College London (UCL), London, UK.

journal_articles.title: Building-block synthesis as a determinant of antibiotic persistence.
journal_articles.abstract: Reduced antibiotic target activity is a major driver of antibiotic treatment failure. While this has mostly been linked to the presence of low-energy bacteria, a recent study by Taher and colleagues suggests that reduced building-block synthesis can also promote antibiotic survival during nitrogen starvation — a route distinct from energy limitation.

last_author.name: Séverin Ronneau
affiliations: INSERM U1230, University of Rennes, Rennes, France. severin.ronneau@univ-rennes.fr.

journal_articles.title: Carbon nanotubes as the supporting film for cryo-EM specimen preparation.
journal_articles.abstract: Specimen preparation is a critical and rate-limiting step in cryo-EM structural analysis, primarily due to challenges posed by the air-water interface. In this study, we introduce carbon nanotubes (CNTs) as a one-dimensional fibrous support material to address this issue. CNTs interact with macromolecules, effectively protecting them from air-water interfaces, and macromolecules arrange themselves around CNTs in various orientations. Furthermore, CNTs biofunctionalized with affinity tags exhibit strong specificity in binding target macromolecules, facilitating direct purification of targets from cell lysates and on-grid assembly of complexes for subsequent cryo-EM analysis. We also demonstrate that CNT grids are compatible with cell culturing, allowing for seamless integration into the cryo-EM characterization workflow for cellular structures. We anticipate that these properties will make the CNT network a promising support for cryo-EM.

journal_articles.title: Cell-type-specific surfaceome profiling of 100-500 isolated cells using a droplet-based Magnetic Affinity Purification System.
journal_articles.abstract: Cell surface proteins represent an important source of biomarkers and therapeutic targets. However, due to the inherent sensitivity limitations of existing technologies, tissue and cell-type-specific surfaceomes remain poorly characterized, especially in the context of human diseases. Here, we present nanoMAPS (nanoscale Magnetic Affinity Purification System), a miniaturized proteomic sample preparation method for surfaceome profiling of as few as 100-500 cells (~100,000-fold lower than existing technologies). By performing magnetic bead-based affinity purification within a single microliter-scale droplet, nanoMAPS significantly improves the recovery of surface proteins and reduces non-specific absorption of intracellular proteins. Application of nanoMAPS to primary human immune cells and mouse plasma cell populations enables robust identification of established cell-type-specific surface markers as well as other proteins selectively enriched in disease-associated immune cell subpopulations. Together, these results establish nanoMAPS as a broadly applicable platform for extending surface proteomics technology to rare primary cells isolated directly from diseased tissues.

journal_articles.title: Characterization of recombinase-based genetic parts and circuits using nanopore sequencing.
journal_articles.abstract: Recombinases are versatile enzymes able to perform the precise insertion, deletion, and rearrangement of DNA and can act as a foundation for programmable genetic logic and memory. Crucial for their use are accurate measurements of function. However, these are often laborious, time-consuming, and costly to collect. To address this, we develop a semi-automated workflow that combines low-cost liquid handling robotics, multiplexed long-read nanopore sequencing, and a supporting computational analysis tool to enable the high-throughput and detailed characterization of recombinase parts and circuits when used in a variety of contexts and organisms. Our approach overcomes the limitations of typically used fluorescence-based assays and is able to monitor temporal dynamics, observe structural changes at nucleotide resolution, and unravel the internal workings of complex multi-state circuits. The ability to scale up and automate genetic circuit characterization is an essential step towards more rigorous biological metrology that can support the construction of predictive models for efficiently engineering biology.

journal_articles.title: Checkerboard-type Zhang-Rice states in overdoped cuprate superconductors.
journal_articles.abstract: Cuprate superconductors remain central to condensed matter physics due to their technological relevance and unconventional, incompletely understood electronic behavior. While the canonical phase diagram and low-energy models have been shaped largely by studies of underdoped and moderately doped cuprates, the overdoped regime has received comparatively limited attention. Here, we track the evolution of the electronic structure from optimal to heavy overdoping in La2-xSrxCuO4 (LSCO) using broadband optical spectroscopy across x = 0.15-0.60. The measured spectral changes-including the redistribution of Zhang-Rice-related spectral weight-are in qualitative agreement with determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations of the three-orbital Emery model, which together indicate a pronounced reconstruction of the electronic structure beyond hole concentrations x > 0.2. Guided by these observations, we propose a spontaneous checkerboard-type Zhang-Rice electronic configuration that accounts for the coexistence of itinerant and localized carriers characteristic of the heavily overdoped state. Our results refine the doping-dependent Zhang-Rice-based framework for cuprates, illuminate how correlations persist deep into the overdoped regime, and provide new constraints on microscopic mechanisms of high-temperature superconductivity, with broader implications for correlated transition-metal oxides.

last_author.name: Xinmao Yin

journal_articles.title: Climate urgency enables political alignment for Latin American power integration.
journal_articles.abstract: Political fragmentation continues to block urgently needed power integration in Latin America, despite the region's vast renewable energy potential. Using the Multiple Streams Approach, this study argues that the escalating climate crisis now acts as a focusing event, aligning a pressing energy problem, viable integration solutions, and growing political will. This alignment signals that a policy window is open. This study combines the Multiple Streams Approach with system modeling to quantify overlooked political costs of inaction, specifically, geopolitical tensions and erosion of trust, offering actionable leverage for policy entrepreneurs. Simulations for 2025-2050 show that continued fragmentation increases system costs by up to 7%, reduces resilience to hydroclimatic shocks, and concentrates benefits within narrow cooperating blocs under low-trust conditions. These measurable and rising costs underscore that regional energy integration is no longer just a technical or economic issue; it is a political imperative. Bold leadership must act now to seize this fleeting window of opportunity.

last_author.name: Rodrigo Moreno

journal_articles.title: Controlled living ring expansion polymerization for the precision synthesis of cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides).
journal_articles.abstract: Cyclic polymers exhibit physical properties distinct from those of their linear polymer counterparts. Although cyclic polymer materials with advanced designs can be synthesized using methods that control their molecular weight, dispersity, and topology, synthetic limitations have thus far restricted structurally defined cyclic polymers to non-conjugated structures with sp³-hybridized carbon backbones. Here we report a living ring expansion polymerization that enables the precise synthesis of cyclic polymers composed of sp²-hybridized carbon backbones, that is, cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides). Polymerization is initiated from a diarylpalladacycle complex in the presence of iodobenzene dichloride and proceeds via the successive insertion of aryl isocyanides into the palladacycle. This living polymerization process yields structurally controlled cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides) with low dispersity and predefined, customizable, high or low-molecular weights. The cyclic topology was unambiguously characterized by multiple analytical techniques, including direct visualization by high-resolution atomic force microscopy. Furthermore, the high fidelity of the palladium center facilitates the controlled synthesis of cyclic block copolymers. This advancement opens avenues for the development of topologically conjugated polymer materials.

journal_articles.title: Controlling the shell growth mechanism and interfacial oxidation of InAs/ZnSe quantum dots for shortwave infrared emission.
journal_articles.abstract: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Furthermore, integrating CQDs into LEDs often introduces severe interfacial quenching and intrinsic charge imbalances. Here we report a highly efficient heavy-metal-free SWIR LED operating at 1525 nm, enabled by tailored injection strategies and oxidation-induced interfacial engineering. Optimized high-temperature ZnCl₂ treatment and continuous precursor injection improve shell nucleation and growth, while controlled interfacial oxidation is associated with reduced shell-thickness-dependent strain signatures and improved PLQY retention during shell thickening. Together, these strategies yield measured PLQYs exceeding 55% for emission beyond 1400 nm. Moreover, we demonstrate that incorporating a semiconducting InAs CQD interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial quenching and regulates electron over-injection. Combined with a doped hole-transport layer to reduce series resistance, our optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 3.5% and a record radiance of ~17 W sr-1 m-2, alongside a T50 operational lifetime of 16 h. Our findings suggest that integrating mechanism-driven shell growth with rational device engineering offers a strategy to overcome current bottlenecks in colloidal emitters, facilitating the transition toward short-wave infrared applications.

journal_articles.title: Coordination-mediated cold quenching for the synthesis of strongly quantum-confined FAPbI3 quantum dots.
journal_articles.abstract: Strong quantum confinement can fundamentally reshape excitonic processes and radiative recombination in perovskite quantum dots (QDs), yet accessing this regime remains challenging in organic-inorganic hybrid FAPbI3 nanocrystals because of their low crystallization barrier and rapid growth. Here, we report a coordination-mediated cold quenching strategy for synthesizing strongly quantum-confined FAPbI3 QDs with tunable emission from 696 to 759 nm. The key step involves the injection of a precooled ethyl methacrylate (EMA, -70 °C), which rapidly lowers the reaction temperature while simultaneously retarding precursor conversion and suppressing QD regrowth. Such a strategy enables small QDs with an average size of 6.4 nm and a near-unity photoluminescence quantum yield. Representative light-emitting diodes based on these QDs deliver electroluminescence at 715 nm with a peak external quantum efficiency of 16.3%. This work provides a viable strategy for accessing ultrasmall hybrid perovskite QDs and advances the rational control of quantum confinement in soft ionic semiconductors.

journal_articles.title: Creation of ferroelectric flux-closure transistor array for non-volatile field-effect memory.
journal_articles.abstract: Ferroelectric flux-closures are promising candidates for high-performance memories, offering reversible switching and low power consumption. However, integration of ferroelectric flux-closures into memory devices is elusive, mostly due to the constraint from the substrate on which polar film is grown. Here, we demonstrate ferroelectric field-effect transistors (Fe-FETs) based on freestanding films with identical polar flux-closures. The retention of flux-closure in the freestanding film is driven by the intrinsic self-organization of polarization to minimize the combined elastic and electrostatic energies. The flux-closure structures exhibit low coercive electric field (Ec), negligible leakage currents, and endurance up to 1010 cycles. Furthermore, the as-fabricated complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible Fe-FET arrays achieve reversible information writing and erasure. They set a benchmark for perovskite-structured devices by simultaneously achieving a large memory window of 0.43 V/nm and a high on/off ratio of 108, while maintaining endurance and stability. Our work paves the way for ferroelectric devices in future semiconductor industries.

journal_articles.title: Cryo-EM sample preparation with soft-landing and laser flash melting.
journal_articles.abstract: The preparation of cryo-EM samples by soft-landing mass spectrometry promises to significantly simplify sample optimization, which has remained an important bottleneck in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo‑EM). However, only compacted configurations are observed after soft-landing since the proteins are dehydrated in the process. Here, we deposit a layer of amorphous ice onto the sample and briefly flash melt it to rehydrate the soft-landed proteins. Melting with a 30 µs laser pulse creates a broad ensemble of partially rehydrated structures. However, a subset of particles returns to a configuration close to the native state. This allows us to propose strategies to fully rehydrate the entire ensemble and brings routine sample preparation by soft-landing mass spectrometry within reach.

journal_articles.title: Cryo-EM structure of ex vivo Sup35 yeast prion and the factors defining prion phenotype.
journal_articles.abstract: Human prions and amyloids exhibit structural diversity that correlates with different pathological manifestations. Yeast prions represent a convenient model for studying fundamental properties of prions and their strain diversity. The Sup35 yeast prion has multiple structural variants, divided into "strong" and "weak" groups differing in frequency of fibril fragmentation and resulting nonsense-suppression. The molecular origin of these distinctions remains unclear. Here, we show that the different frequency of prion fragmentation is determined by their stability, rather than the efficiency of chaperone binding. The fully protease-resistant part (residues 2-32) of the Sup35 prion core is a key for the prion phenotype and maintenance, whereas partially resistant part (33-72) is less important. We established the cryo-EM structure of a strong Sup35 prion variant purified from yeast, comprising residues 2-64, with 2.7 Å resolution. Comparison of this structure with that of Sup35 amyloid formed in vitro at 4˚C revealed their significant difference.

journal_articles.title: Cryo-EM structure of human Na+/H+ exchanger NHA1 in an inward-open conformation.
journal_articles.abstract: The human Na+/H+ exchanger NHA1 (SLC9B1) plays a critical role in sperm motility and male fertility by regulating intracellular pH through its sodium-proton antiport activity. Despite its physiological importance, the structural and mechanistic basis of NHA1 function has remained elusive. Here, we present the cryo-EM structure of human NHA1 at 3.6 Å resolution, captured in an inward-open conformation. Structural comparisons with modeled outward-open states reveal substantial conformational changes in the core domain, supporting an elevator-like transport mechanism. Additionally, several key residues are identified that modify their interaction patterns, likely aiding in the conformational switches necessary for substrate transport. Their contribution to substrate transport is further supported by mutagenesis and sodium transport assays, providing insights into the molecular mechanism of NHA1.

journal_articles.title: Design of white circularly polarized luminescence with high glum across entire visible regions by dual-loop active learning.
journal_articles.abstract: White circularly polarized luminescence (WCPL) materials have attracted increasing attention. However, achieving WCPL simultaneously with high color rendering index (CRI) value at ideal CIE coordinates and large dissymmetry factor (glum) across entire visible regions remains a significant challenging, due to the vast chemical design space and the inefficient experimental screening by human-driven intuition-based methods. Herein, we propose an AI-assisted interactive experiment-learning evolution strategy to accelerate the discovery of WCPL materials with optimal trade-offs, integrating model recommendation, experimental validations, and active learning in each iterative refinement cycle. A multi-objective optimization algorithm automatically guides the experimental design with a dual-loop active learning framework, one for maximizing CRI at ideal CIE coordinates, and the other for optimizing glum value across entire visible regions. High-performance WCPL materials with excellent |glum | (>1.5) range of 410 to 680 nm, high CRI ( > 90) at ideal CIE coordinates (0.33, 0.33) can simultaneously be achieved with limited experimental date. Moreover, this workflow also enables on-demand fabrication of high performance white circularly polarized organic light-emitting diodes as well as the user-specified correlated color temperature, facilitating their application in lighting and full-color 3D display.
